title.zh: 卷五十九 列傳第四十七: 寇洛 趙貴 李賢 梁禦
title.en: Volume 59 Biographies 47: Kou Luo, Zhao Gui, Li Xian, Liang Yu
title.raw: 卷五十九 列傳第四十七: 寇洛 趙貴 李賢 梁禦 Volume 59 Biographies 47: Kou Luo, Zhao Gui, Li Xian, Liang Yu

sentences.zh: 寇洛 趙貴 李賢 梁禦

translations.literal: Kou Luo, Zhao Gui, Li Xian, Liang Yu
translations.idiomatic: Kou Luo; Zhao Gui; Li Xian; and Liang Yu.

sentences.zh: 列傳第四十七

translations.literal: Biographies 47
translations.idiomatic: Biography 47

sentences.zh: 寇洛趙貴從祖兄善李賢子詢崇孫敏弟遠穆穆子渾梁禦子睿

translations.literal: Kou Luo; Zhao Gui; elder cousin Shan; Li Xian; sons Xun and Chong; grandson Min; younger brothers Yuan and Mu; Mu's son Hun; Liang Yu; son Rui
translations.idiomatic: Kou Luo; Zhao Gui; his elder cousin Shan; Li Xian; Li Xian's sons Xun and Chong, grandson Min, and younger brothers Yuan and Mu, and Mu's son Hun; Liang Yu; and Liang Yu's son Rui.

sentences.zh: 寇洛，上穀昌平人也。

translations.literal: Kou Luo was a native of Changping in Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Luo was from Changping in Shanggu commandery.

sentences.zh: 累世為將吏。

translations.literal: For generations his family had served as generals and officials.
translations.idiomatic: His family had produced generals and officials for generations.

sentences.zh: 父延壽，魏和平中，以良家子鎮武川，因家焉。

translations.literal: His father Yan Shou, during the Heping era of Wei, was garrisoned at Wuchuan as a son of a good family, and the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan Shou was posted to garrison Wuchuan during Emperor Xiaowen's Heping reign as a son of a good family, and the clan made its home there.

sentences.zh: 洛性明辯，不拘小節。

translations.literal: Luo was bright and articulate by nature and did not fuss over minor points of etiquette.
translations.idiomatic: Luo was quick-witted and articulate by nature and cared little for petty formalities.

sentences.zh: 賀拔嶽西征，洛與嶽鄉里，乃募從入關。

translations.literal: When Heba Yue marched west on campaign, Luo, being from the same home region as Yue, raised followers to join him in entering Guan.
translations.idiomatic: When Heba Yue marched west, Luo—who was from the same district as Yue—raised men to follow him through the passes into Guan.

sentences.zh: 以功封安鄉縣子。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Anxiang county.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Anxiang.

sentences.zh: 及嶽為大行台，以洛為右都督。

translations.literal: When Yue became Grand Mobile Headquarters, Luo was made right commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue became Grand Mobile Headquarters, Luo was appointed right commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 侯莫陳悅既害嶽，欲並其眾。

translations.literal: After Hou Mo Chen Yue had killed Yue, he wished to absorb his forces.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hou Mo Chen Yue had killed Yue, he sought to take over his army.

sentences.zh: 時初喪元帥，洛于諸將中最為舊齒，素為眾信，乃收集將士，志在復讎。

translations.literal: They had just lost their commander-in-chief; among the generals Luo was the senior in years and had long been trusted by all, so he gathered officers and soldiers, his aim being revenge.
translations.idiomatic: The army had just lost its commander; of all the generals Luo was the senior and had long enjoyed the men's trust, so he rallied the troops with revenge in mind.

sentences.zh: 既至原州，眾推洛為盟主，統嶽之眾，至平涼。

translations.literal: When they reached Yuanzhou, the host made Luo their covenant leader, commandeering Yue's forces, and they advanced to Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuanzhou the troops chose Luo as covenant leader, took command of Yue's forces, and marched on to Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 周文帝至，以洛為右都督。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou arrived, Luo was made right commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou arrived, Luo was again appointed right commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 從討侯莫陳悅，平之。

translations.literal: He followed in campaigning against Hou Mo Chen Yue and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the campaign against Hou Mo Chen Yue and brought him down.

sentences.zh: 拜涇州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed governor of Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor of Jing province.

sentences.zh: 大統初，詔加開府，進爵京兆郡公，封洛母宋為襄城郡君。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, an edict added the opening of a government office, raised his rank to Duke of Jingzhao commandery, and ennobled Luo's mother, née Song, as Lady of Xiangcheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Datong era an edict granted him an opened government office, raised him to Duke of Jingzhao, and ennobled his mother, Lady Song, as Lady of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 四年，鎮東雍州。

translations.literal: In year 4 he was assigned to garrison eastern Yong province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was posted to garrison eastern Yong province.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒於鎮，贈太尉、尚書令，諡曰武。

translations.literal: In year 5 he died at his post; posthumously he was given Grand Commandant and Director of the Imperial Secretariat, with the posthumous title Martial.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died on duty; he was posthumously made Grand Commandant and Director of the Imperial Secretariat, with the posthumous name Martial.

sentences.zh: 子和嗣。

translations.literal: His son He inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son He succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 明帝二年，錄舊勳，以洛配享文帝廟庭，賜和姓若引氏，改封松陽郡公。

translations.literal: In year 2 of Emperor Ming, recording former merit, Luo was given collateral worship in the temple court of Emperor Wen, granted the surname Ruo Yin of the He clan, and his fief was changed to Duke of Songyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Ming, when former merit was recorded, Luo was given collateral worship in Emperor Wen's temple, granted the surname Ruo Yin of the imperial clan, and his title was changed to Duke of Songyang.

sentences.zh: 趙貴，字元寶，天水南安人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Gui, style Yuanbao, was a native of Nan'an in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gui, courtesy name Yuanbao, was a native of Nan'an in Tianshui commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖仁，以良家子鎮武川，因家焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ren, as a son of a good family, was garrisoned at Wuchuan and the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ren was posted to garrison Wuchuan as a son of a good family, and the family settled there.

sentences.zh: 貴少有節概，爾硃榮以為別將，從討元顥有功，賜爵燕樂縣子。

translations.literal: Gui in youth had integrity and mettle; Erzhu Rong made him a separate general, and following the campaign against Yuan Hao he had merit and was granted the title Viscount of Yanle county.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Gui showed integrity and spirit; Erzhu Rong appointed him a separate general, and in the campaign against Yuan Hao he distinguished himself and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Yanle.

sentences.zh: 從賀拔岳平關中，累遷大都督。

translations.literal: Following Heba Yue he pacified Guanzhong and was repeatedly promoted to grand commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Heba Yue in pacifying Guanzhong and rose through repeated promotions to grand commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 岳為侯莫陳悅所害，將吏奔敗，莫有守者。

translations.literal: Yue was killed by Hou Mo Chen Yue; officers and clerks fled and collapsed; none held their posts.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue was killed by Hou Mo Chen Yue, officers and clerks scattered in defeat and no one held the line.

sentences.zh: 謂其黨曰：「吾聞仁義豈有常哉，行之則為君子，違之則為小人。

translations.literal: He said to his comrades: "I have heard that benevolence and righteousness have no fixed form—practice them and you are a gentleman; violate them and you are a petty man.
translations.idiomatic: He said to his followers, "I have heard that benevolence and righteousness have no fixed rule—live by them and you are a gentleman; turn from them and you are a base man.

sentences.zh: 硃伯厚、王修感意氣微恩，尚能蹈履名節，況吾等荷賀拔公國士之遇，寧可自同眾人乎？」

translations.literal: Zhu Boxhou and Wang Xiu were stirred by a slight debt of honor and still could walk the path of renown and integrity; how much more we, who bore Lord Heba's treatment as men of the state's esteem—could we make ourselves like the common crowd?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Boxhou and Wang Xiu, moved by a trifling debt of honor, still upheld their reputations and integrity; how much more should we, who received from Lord Heba the treatment due a man of the state's esteem, make ourselves no better than the common run?"

sentences.zh: 因涕泣噓唏，從之者五十人。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wept and sobbed, and fifty men followed him.
translations.idiomatic: With that he wept aloud, and fifty men followed him.

sentences.zh: 乃詣悅詐降，悅信之。

translations.literal: He then went to Yue and feigned surrender; Yue believed him.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Hou Mo Chen Yue and pretended to surrender, and Yue believed him.

sentences.zh: 因請收葬嶽，言辭慷慨，悅壯而許之。

translations.literal: He then asked to collect and bury Yue; his words were impassioned, and Yue, impressed, granted it.
translations.idiomatic: He asked permission to recover and bury Yue's body, speaking with such fervor that Yue was moved and consented.

sentences.zh: 貴乃收岳屍還營，與寇洛等奔平涼，共圖拒悅。

translations.literal: Gui then recovered Yue's corpse and returned to camp; with Kou Luo and others he fled to Pingliang to plan resistance to Yue together.
translations.idiomatic: Gui recovered Yue's body and returned to camp, then fled with Kou Luo and the rest to Pingliang to plot resistance against Hou Mo Chen Yue.

sentences.zh: 貴乃首議迎周文帝。

translations.literal: Gui was the first to propose welcoming Emperor Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was the first to propose welcoming Emperor Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 周文至，以貴為大都督，領府司馬。

translations.literal: When Zhou Wen arrived, Gui was made grand commander-in-chief and head of the headquarters marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou arrived, Gui was made grand commander-in-chief and placed in charge of the headquarters marshal's office.

sentences.zh: 悅平，行秦州事。

translations.literal: When Yue was pacified, he acted as administrator of Qin province.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Mo Chen Yue was defeated, Gui acted as administrator of Qin province.

sentences.zh: 後以預立魏文帝勳，進爵為公。

translations.literal: Later, for his part in establishing Emperor Wen of Wei, his rank was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for his role in enthroning Emperor Wen of Wei, he was raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 梁ＧＣ定稱亂河右，以貴為隴西行台討破之。

translations.literal: Liang Qiding proclaimed rebellion in the lands west of the Yellow River; Gui was made mobile headquarters of Longxi and led troops to campaign against and break him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Qiding rebelled west of the river, Gui was made Longxi mobile headquarters commander and crushed him.

sentences.zh: 從復弘農，戰沙苑，進爵中山郡公。

translations.literal: He followed in recovering Hongnong and fought at Shaya, and his rank was advanced to Duke of Zhongshan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in recovering Hongnong and fighting at Shaya, and was raised to Duke of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 河橋之戰，貴與怡峰為左軍，戰不利，先還。

translations.literal: At the battle of Heqiao, Gui and Yi Feng were the left army; the battle went badly and they returned first.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Heqiao, Gui and Yi Feng commanded the left wing; the fight went badly and they withdrew first.

sentences.zh: 及高仲密以北豫州降，周文迎之，與東魏人戰於芒山。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhongmi surrendered with northern Yuzhou, Zhou Wen went to welcome him and fought Eastern Wei forces at Mangshan.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi surrendered northern Yuzhou, Emperor Wen of Zhou went to receive him and fought Eastern Wei at Mangshan.

sentences.zh: 貴為左軍，失律，坐免官。

translations.literal: Gui was on the left army, violated military discipline, and was dismissed from office on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Gui commanded the left wing but broke discipline and was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 尋復官爵。

translations.literal: Before long his office and title were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his rank and office were restored.

sentences.zh: 後拜柱國大將軍，賜姓乙弗氏。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed pillar-of-state grand general and granted the surname Yifu.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made pillar-of-state grand general and granted the surname Yifu.

sentences.zh: 六官建，為太保、大宗伯，改封南陽郡公。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he became Grand Guardian and Grand Clan Elder, and his fief was changed to Duke of Nanyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established, he became Grand Guardian and Grand Clan Elder, and his title was changed to Duke of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，遷大塚宰，進封楚國公，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, Gui was moved to Grand Overseer of the Ancestral Temple, advanced to Duke of the state of Chu, with a fief of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, Gui was made Grand Overseer of the Ancestral Temple, raised to Duke of Chu, with a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 初，貴與獨孤信等皆與文帝等夷。

translations.literal: At first Gui, Dugu Xin, and the others were equals of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: At first Gui, Dugu Xin, and the others had stood on equal footing with Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 及晉公護攝政，貴自以元勳，每懷怏怏，與信謀殺護，為開府宇文盛告，被誅。

translations.literal: When Duke of Jin Hu took the regency, Gui, considering himself a founding merit-holder, was resentful; he plotted with Xin to kill Hu, was denounced by Acting Three Excellencies Yuwen Sheng, and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu became regent, Gui, counting himself a founding merit-holder, grew resentful; he plotted with Dugu Xin to kill Hu, was reported by Acting Three Excellencies Yuwen Sheng, and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 善，字僧慶，貴之從祖兄也。

translations.literal: Shan, style Sengqing, was Gui's elder cousin on the paternal side.
translations.idiomatic: Shan, courtesy name Sengqing, was Zhao Gui's elder cousin on the paternal side.

sentences.zh: 少好學，美容儀，沉毅有遠量。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning, had a handsome bearing, and was steady and resolute with far-reaching judgment.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved learning, was handsome in bearing, and was steady and far-sighted.

sentences.zh: 爾硃天光討邢杲、万俟醜奴，以為長史。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Tianguang campaigned against Xing Gao and Moqi Chounu, Shan was made chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Tianguang campaigned against Xing Gao and Moqi Chounu, Shan served as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，為大行台尚書，封山北縣伯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai he was Grand Mobile Headquarters Director of the Imperial Secretariat and was enfeoffed as Earl of Shanbei county.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Putai era he became Director of the Imperial Secretariat under the Grand Mobile Headquarters and was enfeoffed as Earl of Shanbei.

sentences.zh: 天光拒齊神武于韓陵，敗，見殺。

translations.literal: Tianguang resisted Gao Huan of Northern Qi at Hanling, was defeated, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang met Gao Huan at Hanling, was defeated, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 善請收葬其屍，齊神武義而許之。

translations.literal: Shan asked to collect and bury his corpse; Gao Huan, moved by righteousness, granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Shan asked to recover and bury his body; Gao Huan, approving the request on grounds of righteousness, allowed it.

sentences.zh: 賀拔嶽總關中，迎善，復以為長史。

translations.literal: When Heba Yue took overall command of Guanzhong, he welcomed Shan and again made him chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Heba Yue took command of Guanzhong, he welcomed Shan back and again appointed him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 岳為侯莫陳悅所殺，善共諸將翊戴周文帝。

translations.literal: When Yue was killed by Hou Mo Chen Yue, Shan together with the generals supported and installed Emperor Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue was killed by Hou Mo Chen Yue, Shan and the other generals rallied to support Emperor Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武西遷，改封襄城縣伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Shan's fief was changed to Earl of Xiangcheng county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Shan's title was changed to Earl of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 歷位尚書左右僕射，進爵為公。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of left and right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat and was advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of left and right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat and was advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 善性溫恭，有器局，雖位居端右，而愈自謙退。

translations.literal: Shan was mild and respectful by nature and had breadth of vision; though he stood at the highest rank, he became all the more self-effacing.
translations.idiomatic: Shan was gentle and courteous by nature and possessed real breadth of vision; though he held the highest offices, he grew only more modest.

sentences.zh: 其職務克舉，則曰某官之力；

translations.literal: When duties were successfully performed, he would say it was that official's merit;
translations.idiomatic: When a task was well done, he would say it was that official's achievement;

sentences.zh: 有罪責，則曰善之咎也。

translations.literal: when there was guilt or blame, he would say it was Shan's fault.
translations.idiomatic: when there was fault or blame, he would say the fault was his own.

sentences.zh: 時人稱其有公輔量。

translations.literal: People of the time said he had the capacity of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries said he had the makings of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 大統九年，從戰芒山，屬大軍不利，善為敵所獲，卒於東魏。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Datong he followed the battle at Mangshan; as the great army fared badly, Shan was captured by the enemy and died in Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Datong he fought at Mangshan; when the main army fared badly, Shan was taken by the enemy and died in Eastern Wei territory.

sentences.zh: 建德初，周、齊通好，齊人乃歸其柩。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiande, Zhou and Qi were on friendly terms, and the Qi people then returned his coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiande era, when Zhou and Qi were on friendly terms, the Qi returned his coffin.

sentences.zh: 其子詢表請贈諡。

translations.literal: His son Xun memorialized requesting a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun submitted a memorial requesting a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 詔贈大將軍、大都督、四州諸軍事、岐州刺史，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him Grand General, Grand Commander-in-Chief, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Four Provinces, and Governor of Qi province, with the posthumous title Reverent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him Grand General, Grand Commander-in-Chief, commander of military affairs in four provinces, and governor of Qi, with the posthumous name Reverent.

sentences.zh: 李賢，字賢和，自雲隴西成紀人，漢騎都尉陵之後也。

translations.literal: Li Xian, style Xianhe, claimed to be from Chengji in Longxi and was a descendant of Han Cavalry Commandant Li Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian, courtesy name Xianhe, claimed descent from Chengji in Longxi and from Han Cavalry Commandant Li Ling.

sentences.zh: 陵沒匈奴，子孫因居北狄。

translations.literal: Ling perished among the Xiongnu, and his descendants therefore lived among the northern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When Ling was lost among the Xiongnu, his descendants settled among the northern peoples.

sentences.zh: 後隨魏南遷，復歸汧、隴。

translations.literal: Later they followed Wei in moving south and returned to Qian and Long.
translations.idiomatic: Later they followed the Wei court south and returned to the Qian and Long region.

sentences.zh: 曾祖富，魏太武時以子都督討兩山屠各，歿於陣，贈甯西將軍、隴西郡守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Fu, in the time of Emperor Taiwu of Wei, as a sub-commander campaigned against the Tuge of Liangshan, died in battle, and was posthumously given General Who Pacifies the West and Administrator of Longxi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Fu, under Emperor Taiwu of Wei, campaigned as a sub-commander against the Tuge of Liangshan, fell in battle, and was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the West and administrator of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 大統末，以賢兄弟著勳，追贈司空公。

translations.literal: At the end of Datong, because the Xian brothers had outstanding merit, he was posthumously given Duke of the Excellency of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Datong era, because the Xian brothers had distinguished themselves, Fu was posthumously made Duke of the Excellency of Works.

sentences.zh: 賢幼有志節，不妄舉動。

translations.literal: Xian in youth had resolve and integrity and did not act rashly.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Xian showed resolve and restraint and never acted rashly.

sentences.zh: 嘗出遊，逢一老人，鬢眉皓白，謂曰：「我年八十，觀士多矣，未有如卿。

translations.literal: Once on an outing he met an old man with snow-white temples and brows, who said to him: "I am eighty years old and have observed many gentlemen, yet none like you.
translations.idiomatic: Once while out walking he met an old man with white temples and brows who said, "I am eighty and have seen many men of talent, but none like you.

sentences.zh: 卿必為臺牧，努力勉之。」

translations.literal: You will surely become a terrace governor; strive and encourage yourself."
translations.idiomatic: You are sure to become a provincial governor—work hard at it."

sentences.zh: 九歲，從師受業，略觀大指而已。

translations.literal: At age nine he followed a teacher in study, merely surveying the main points.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he began study under a teacher, but only skimmed the main outlines.

sentences.zh: 或譏其不精，答曰：「賢豈能領徒授業？

translations.literal: Some mocked him for lack of mastery; he replied: "How could Xian lead disciples and teach a profession?
translations.idiomatic: When some mocked his lack of mastery, he replied, "How could Xian lead pupils and teach for a living?

sentences.zh: 至如忠孝之道，實銘於心。」

translations.literal: As for the way of loyalty and filial piety, it is truly engraved in my heart."
translations.idiomatic: As for the way of loyalty and filial piety, that is engraved in my heart."

sentences.zh: 問者慚服。

translations.literal: Those who had questioned him were ashamed and convinced.
translations.idiomatic: His questioners were ashamed and silenced.

sentences.zh: 十四遭父憂，撫訓諸弟，友愛甚篤。

translations.literal: At fourteen he suffered his father's death, reared and instructed his younger brothers, and was deeply affectionate toward them.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he lost his father, raised and guided his younger brothers, and showed them deep affection.

sentences.zh: 魏永安中，萬俊醜奴據岐、涇等州反，孝莊遣爾硃天光擊破之。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era of Wei, Moqi Chounu held Qi, Jing, and other provinces in rebellion; Emperor Xiaozhuang sent Erzhu Tianguang to campaign against and break him.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Xiaozhuang's Yong'an reign, Moqi Chounu rebelled holding Qi, Jing, and other provinces; the emperor sent Erzhu Tianguang, who defeated him.

sentences.zh: 天光令都督長孫邪利行原州事，以賢為主簿。

translations.literal: Tianguang ordered Commander-in-Chief Zhangsun Xieli to act as administrator of Yuan province affairs and made Xian chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang put Commander Zhangsun Xieli in charge of Yuan province and made Xian his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 累遷高平令。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to magistrate of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through promotion to magistrate of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 賀拔岳為侯莫陳悅所害，周文帝西征，賢與其弟遠、穆等密應侯莫陳崇。

translations.literal: When Heba Yue was killed by Hou Mo Chen Yue, Emperor Wen of Zhou marched west on campaign; Xian with his younger brothers Yuan and Mu and others secretly responded to Hou Mo Chen Chong.
translations.idiomatic: After Heba Yue was killed by Hou Mo Chen Yue, Emperor Wen of Zhou marched west; Xian and his brothers Yuan and Mu secretly supported Hou Mo Chen Chong.

sentences.zh: 以功授都督，仍守原州。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted the title commander-in-chief and still guarded Yuan province.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made commander-in-chief and continued to hold Yuan province.

sentences.zh: 及大軍至秦州，悅棄城走。

translations.literal: When the great army reached Qin province, Yue abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army reached Qin province, Hou Mo Chen Yue abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 周文命兄子導追之，以賢為先鋒，至牽屯山及之。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen ordered his elder brother's son Dao to pursue; Xian was made vanguard, and at Qian Tun mountain they caught up with him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen ordered his nephew Dao to pursue; Xian led the vanguard and caught up with Yue at Qian Tun Mountain.

sentences.zh: 以功授假節、撫軍將軍、大都督。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted acting credentials, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Grand Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was granted acting credentials, the title General Who Pacifies the Army, and grand commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 武帝及齊王憲之在繈褓，不利居宮中，周文令於賢家處之，六載乃還宮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu and Prince of Qi Xian were in swaddling clothes, it was inauspicious for them to dwell in the palace; Zhou Wen had them lodged in Xian's household, and only after six years did they return to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Wu and Prince Xian of Qi were still infants, it was deemed ill-omened for them to live in the palace; Emperor Wen placed them in Xian's household, and only after six years did they return to court.

sentences.zh: 因賜賢妻吳姓宇文氏，養為侄女，賜與甚厚。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xian's wife, née Wu, was granted the surname Yuwen, raised as a niece [of the imperial clan], and given lavish gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's wife, Lady Wu, was granted the surname Yuwen, adopted as an imperial niece, and showered with gifts.

sentences.zh: 及武帝西巡原州，幸賢第，詔曰：「朕昔沖幼，爰寓此州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu toured Yuan province on his western progress and visited Xian's residence, an edict said: "I was once young and tender and made my home in this province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu toured west to Yuan province and visited Xian's home, he issued an edict saying, "In my youth I lived in this province.

sentences.zh: 使持節、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、大都督、瓜州諸軍事、瓜州刺史賢，斯土良家，勳德兼著，受委居朕，輔導積年。

translations.literal: Bearer of credentials, Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Acting Three Excellencies with Court Equipage, Grand Commander-in-Chief, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Guazhou, and Governor of Guazhou—Xian, a son of a good family of this land, with merit and virtue both outstanding, was entrusted to attend me and guided me for many years.
translations.idiomatic: Bearer of credentials, Grand General of Fast Cavalry, acting three excellencies with court equipage, grand commander-in-chief, commander of military affairs in Guazhou, and governor of Guazhou—Xian, a worthy son of this region, distinguished in merit and virtue, was entrusted with my care and instructed me for many years.

sentences.zh: 念其規弼，功勞甚茂。

translations.literal: Reflecting on his guidance and assistance, his service and toil have been very abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering his guidance, his service has been abundant indeed.

sentences.zh: 今巡撫屆此，不殊代邑，舉目依然，益增舊想。

translations.literal: Now on my tour of inspection I have come here; it is no different from the place of my youth—every sight is as before, and my old feelings only increase.
translations.idiomatic: Now on my tour I have come here; it is no different from the place of my youth—every sight is unchanged, and my old memories only grow stronger.

sentences.zh: 賢雖無屬籍，朕處之若親，凡厥昆季，乃至子侄等，可並預宴賜。」

translations.literal: Though Xian has no entry in the clan register, I treat him as kin; all his brothers, down to sons and nephews, may alike share in the feast and gifts."
translations.idiomatic: Though Xian is not on the imperial register, I treat him as family; all his brothers, sons, and nephews alike may share in the feast and gifts."

sentences.zh: 於是令中侍上士尉遲愷往瓜州，降璽書勞賢。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Palace Attendant Senior Gentleman Yuchi Kai to go to Guazhou and issue an imperial letter of commendation to Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Palace Attendant Senior Gentleman Yuchi Kai to Guazhou with an imperial letter commending Xian.

sentences.zh: 賜衣一襲及被褥，並禦所服十三環金帶一腰、中廄馬一疋、金裝鞍勒、雜彩五百段、銀錢一萬。

translations.literal: He was granted one suit of clothing and bedding, together with one thirteen-ring gold belt worn by the emperor, one horse from the central stud, gold-mounted saddle and bridle, five hundred bolts of mixed silks, and ten thousand in silver cash.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a suit of clothes and bedding, the emperor's own thirteen-ring gold belt, a horse from the imperial stables with gold-mounted saddle and bridle, five hundred bolts of mixed silks, and ten thousand in silver cash.

sentences.zh: 賜賢弟申國公穆亦如之。

translations.literal: Xian's younger brother Mu, Duke of the state of Shen, was granted the same.
translations.idiomatic: The same gifts were given to Xian's younger brother Mu, Duke of Shen.

sentences.zh: 子侄男女中外諸孫三十四人各賜衣一襲。

translations.literal: Thirty-four sons, nephews, male and female, and grandsons within and outside the clan each received one suit of clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-four sons, nephews, and grandsons by blood and marriage each received a suit of clothes.

sentences.zh: 拜賢甥庫狄樂為儀同。

translations.literal: Xian's nephew by marriage, Kudi Le, was appointed Acting Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's nephew by marriage Kudi Le was appointed acting three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 賢門生昔經侍奉者，二人授大都督，四人授帥都督，六人別將。

translations.literal: Of Xian's disciples who had formerly attended him, two were granted grand commander-in-chief, four were granted commander-in-chief of the host, and six were made separate generals.
translations.idiomatic: Of Xian's former disciples who had served him, two were made grand commanders-in-chief, four commanders-in-chief of the host, and six separate generals.

sentences.zh: 奴已免賤者五人，授軍主；

translations.literal: Five slaves who had already been freed from servile status were granted the rank of army leader;
translations.idiomatic: Five former slaves who had already been freed were made army leaders;

sentences.zh: 未免賤者十二人，酬替放之。

translations.literal: Twelve who had not yet been freed from servile status were compensated in replacement and released.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve who had not yet been freed from bondage were paid off and released.

sentences.zh: 四年，王師東討，西道空虛，慮羌、渾侵擾，乃授賢河州總管。

translations.literal: In year 4, when the royal army marched east on campaign and the western route was empty, fearing Qiang and Hun raids, Xian was appointed area commander of He province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, as the imperial army marched east and the western frontier lay exposed, fearing raids by the Qiang and Hun, Xian was made area commander of He province.

sentences.zh: 河州舊非總管，至是創置。

translations.literal: He province had not previously had an area commander; one was now created for the first time.
translations.idiomatic: He province had never before had an area command; one was established for the first time on this occasion.

sentences.zh: 賢乃大營屯田，以省運漕，多設斥候，以備寇戎，於是羌、渾斂跡。

translations.literal: Xian then greatly established garrison farming to save on transport grain, set out many scouts to guard against enemy barbarians, and the Qiang and Hun then restrained themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Xian then established large-scale garrison farms to cut transport costs, posted many scouts against raiders, and the Qiang and Hun thereafter kept their distance.

sentences.zh: 五年，宕昌寇邊，乃於洮州置總管府以鎮遏之。

translations.literal: In year 5, Dangchang raided the border, so an area command headquarters was established at Tao province to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when Dangchang raided the frontier, an area command headquarters was set up at Tao province to hold them in check.

sentences.zh: 遂廢河州總管，改授賢洮州總管。

translations.literal: The He province area command was then abolished, and Xian was reassigned as area commander of Tao province.
translations.idiomatic: The He province command was then abolished, and Xian was reassigned as area commander of Tao province.

sentences.zh: 屬羌寇侵擾，賢頻破之，虜遂震懾，不敢犯塞。

translations.literal: When Qiang bandits raided and harassed, Xian repeatedly defeated them; the barbarians were awestruck and did not dare violate the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiang raiders struck repeatedly, Xian defeated them again and again until the enemy was awestruck and dared not breach the border.

sentences.zh: 俄廢洮州總管，還于河州置總管府，復以賢為之。

translations.literal: Soon the Tao province area command was abolished; an area command headquarters was restored at He province, and Xian was again put in charge.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Tao command was abolished, the headquarters was moved back to He province, and Xian was again appointed to it.

sentences.zh: 武帝思賢舊恩，徵拜大將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou, remembering Xian's old kindness, summoned and appointed him Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou, mindful of Xian's past service, summoned him and appointed him Grand General.

sentences.zh: 于京師薨，帝親入，哀動左右。

translations.literal: He died at the capital; the emperor personally entered, and his grief moved those around him.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the capital; the emperor came in person to mourn, and his grief moved all who were present.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、柱國大將軍、大都督、十州諸軍事、原州刺史，諡曰桓。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff, Pillar of State, Grand General, Grand Commander, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs for Ten Provinces, and Governor of Yuan province; posthumous title Huan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the staff of authority, the ranks of Pillar of State and Grand General, the title Grand Commander over military affairs in ten provinces, and the governorship of Yuan province, with the posthumous name Huan.

sentences.zh: 子端嗣。

translations.literal: His son Duan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Duan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 端位開府儀同三司，從平齊，戰沒，贈上大將軍，追封襄陽公，諡曰果。

translations.literal: Duan held the rank of Opening-the-Fu with Pillar-of-State-equivalent Three Excellencies; he followed in the pacification of Qi, fell in battle, was posthumously granted Senior Grand General, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangyang, posthumous title Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Duan held the rank of Opening-the-Fu with Pillar-of-State-equivalent Three Excellencies; he took part in the conquest of Qi, fell in battle, and was posthumously made Senior Grand General and Duke of Xiangyang, with the posthumous name Guo.

sentences.zh: 端弟吉，儀同三司。

translations.literal: Duan's younger brother Ji held Pillar-of-State-equivalent Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Duan's younger brother Ji held Pillar-of-State-equivalent Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 吉弟孝軌，開府儀同大將軍、升遷縣伯，後封奇章公。

translations.literal: Ji's younger brother Xiaogui was Grand General with Opening-the-Fu and Pillar-of-State-equivalent rank, Earl of Shengqian county, later enfeoffed as Duke of Qizhang.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's younger brother Xiaogui was Grand General with Opening-the-Fu and Pillar-of-State-equivalent rank, Earl of Shengqian, and was later enfeoffed as Duke of Qizhang.

sentences.zh: 孝軌弟詢。

translations.literal: Xiaogui's younger brother Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogui's younger brother was Xun.

sentences.zh: 詢，字孝詢，深沉有大略，頗涉書記。

translations.literal: Xun, courtesy name Xiaoxun, was deep and reserved with great strategy and had considerable learning in letters and records.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, courtesy name Xiaoxun, was deep and reserved, possessed great strategic insight, and was well versed in letters and records.

sentences.zh: 仕周，累遷司衛上士。

translations.literal: He served Zhou and was repeatedly promoted to Senior Attendant of the Guard Office.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Zhou court and rose through repeated promotions to Senior Attendant of the Guard Office.

sentences.zh: 武帝幸雲陽宮，委以留府事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu visited the Cloud Yang Palace, he was entrusted with remaining at the capital to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu visited the Cloud Yang Palace, Xun was entrusted with affairs at the capital in his absence.

sentences.zh: 衛王直作亂，焚肅章門，詢於內益火，故賊不得入。

translations.literal: Prince Wei Zhi rebelled and burned the Su Zhang Gate; Xun set additional fires inside, so the rebels could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wei Zhi rebelled and burned the Su Zhang Gate, Xun set counterfires inside the palace, preventing the rebels from breaking in.

sentences.zh: 武帝善之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 累遷英果中大夫，屢以軍功，加位大將軍，賜爵平高郡公。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Heroic Outstanding Senior Grandee; through repeated military merit he was raised to Grand General and granted the title Duke of Pinggao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to Heroic Outstanding Senior Grandee, and through repeated military merit was raised to Grand General and enfeoffed as Duke of Pinggao.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝為丞相，尉遲迥作亂，遣韋孝寬擊之，以詢為元帥長史，委以心膂。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was Chancellor, Yuchi Jiong rebelled; he dispatched Wei Xiaokuan to attack him and made Xun marshal chief of staff, entrusting him as his right-hand man.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was still Chancellor, Yuchi Jiong rebelled; he sent Wei Xiaokuan against him and made Xun marshal chief of staff, trusting him as his right-hand man.

sentences.zh: 軍至永橋，諸將不一。

translations.literal: When the army reached Yong Bridge, the generals were not of one mind.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Yong Bridge, the generals could not agree.

sentences.zh: 詢密啟請重臣監護。

translations.literal: Xun secretly memorialized requesting that a senior minister supervise the army.
translations.idiomatic: Xun secretly memorialized asking that a senior minister be sent to supervise the army.

sentences.zh: 文帝令高熲監軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen ordered Gao Jiong to supervise the army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen ordered Gao Jiong to take command of supervision over the army.

sentences.zh: 與熲同心，唯詢而已。

translations.literal: Of one mind with Gao Jiong, there was only Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong had only one true ally of one mind with him—Xun.

sentences.zh: 及迥平，進位上柱國，改封隴西郡公。

translations.literal: When Jiong was pacified, he was promoted to Senior Pillar of State and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Longxi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiong was defeated, Xun was promoted to Senior Pillar of State and his title was changed to Duke of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，歷位隰州總管，以疾征還京師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, he successively served as area commander of Xi province, then was summoned back to the capital on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang era he served as area commander of Xi province, then was recalled to the capital because of illness.

sentences.zh: 卒，帝悼惜者久之，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: He died; the emperor mourned him for a long time; posthumous title Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died; the emperor mourned him at length, and gave him the posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 子元方嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yuanfang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanfang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝為丞相，加授上開府儀同大將軍、懷州刺史，進爵郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was Chancellor, Chong was additionally granted Senior Opening-the-Fu Grand General and Governor of Huai province, and advanced to Duke of a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was Chancellor, Chong was additionally made Senior Opening-the-Fu Grand General and Governor of Huai province, and advanced to commandery duke.

sentences.zh: 尉遲迥反，遣使招之。

translations.literal: Yuchi Jiong rebelled and sent envoys to recruit him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jiong rebelled and sent envoys to win him over.

sentences.zh: 崇初欲相應，後知叔父穆以并州附文帝，慨然太息曰：「闔家富貴數十人，遇國有難，竟不能扶傾繼絕，何面目處天地間乎！」

translations.literal: Chong at first wished to respond, but when he learned his uncle Mu had joined Emperor Wen at Bingzhou, he sighed deeply and said: "Our whole household of several dozen men in wealth and honor—when the state faces peril, we cannot shore up the tottering and continue the line. With what face can we stand between heaven and earth!
translations.idiomatic: Chong at first meant to join Jiong, but when he learned that his uncle Mu had sided with Emperor Wen at Bingzhou, he sighed and said, "Our whole clan counts dozens in wealth and rank—yet when the state is in peril we cannot shore up what is falling or carry on what is broken. With what face can we remain under heaven and earth!

sentences.zh: 韋孝寬亦疑之，與俱臥起。

translations.literal: Wei Xiaokuan also suspected him and stayed with him, rising and retiring together.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaokuan also distrusted him and kept him under close watch, sharing his bed and board.

sentences.zh: 其兄詢時為元帥長史，每諷諭之。

translations.literal: His elder brother Xun was then marshal chief of staff and repeatedly exhorted him.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Xun, then marshal chief of staff, repeatedly urged him to do right.

sentences.zh: 崇由是亦歸心焉。

translations.literal: Chong thereby gave his loyalty as well.
translations.idiomatic: Chong thereby gave his loyalty as well.

sentences.zh: 及迥平，授徐州總管，進位上柱國。

translations.literal: When Jiong was pacified, he was appointed area commander of Xu province and promoted to Senior Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiong was defeated, Chong was appointed area commander of Xu province and promoted to Senior Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 開皇三年，除幽州總管。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaihuang, he was appointed area commander of You province.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaihuang he was appointed area commander of You province.

sentences.zh: 突厥犯塞，崇輒破之。

translations.literal: When the Turks raided the frontier, Chong always defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Turks raided the frontier, Chong defeated them.

sentences.zh: 奚、霄、契丹等讋嚇其威略，爭來內附。

translations.literal: The Xi, Kumo Xi, Khitan, and others were awed and frightened by his martial prowess and vied to submit and join the empire.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi, Kumo Xi, Khitan, and other peoples were awed by his martial reputation and vied to submit and join the empire.

sentences.zh: 後突厥大為侵掠，崇率步騎三千拒之。

translations.literal: Later the Turks raided on a large scale; Chong led three thousand infantry and cavalry to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Turks launched a major raid; Chong led three thousand foot and horse to resist them.

sentences.zh: 轉戰十餘日，師人多死，遂保於沙城。

translations.literal: After more than ten days of shifting battle, many of his troops died; he then held out in Sha fortress.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten days of fighting, most of his men were dead, and he withdrew to hold Sha fortress.

sentences.zh: 突厥圍之，死亡略盡。

translations.literal: The Turks besieged it, and nearly all perished.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks besieged the fortress until nearly all inside were dead.

sentences.zh: 突厥欲降之，謂曰：「降者封為特勤。」

translations.literal: The Turks wished to accept his surrender and said to him: "If you surrender, you will be enfeoffed as tegin.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks offered to accept his surrender, saying, "Surrender, and you will be enfeoffed as tegin.

sentences.zh: 崇知不免，令其士卒曰：「吾喪師徒，罪當萬死，今效命以謝國家。

translations.literal: Chong knew he could not escape and told his troops: "I have lost my army and deserve ten thousand deaths; now I shall give my life to repay the state.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not escape, Chong told his men, "I have lost my army and deserve death ten thousand times over; now I shall give my life to repay the state.

sentences.zh: 看吾死，且可降賊，方便散走。

translations.literal: Watch me die; then you may surrender to the enemy and disperse as best you can.
translations.idiomatic: Watch me die; then you may surrender to the enemy and make your escape as best you can.

sentences.zh: 還見至尊，道此意也。」

translations.literal: When you return and see His Majesty, tell him this.
translations.idiomatic: When you return to the emperor, tell him what I have said.

sentences.zh: 乃挺刃突賊，復殺二人，沒於陣。

translations.literal: He then grasped his blade and charged the enemy, killing two more men before falling on the field.
translations.idiomatic: Then he drew his blade and charged the enemy, killed two more men, and fell on the battlefield.

sentences.zh: 主州諸軍事、豫州刺史，諡曰壯。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs for the province and Governor of Yu province; posthumous title Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted command over military affairs in the province and the governorship of Yu province, with the posthumous name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子敏嗣。

translations.literal: His son Min succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Min succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 敏字樹生，文帝以其父死王事，養于宮中。

translations.literal: Min, courtesy name Shusheng; because his father died in service to the throne, he was raised in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Min, courtesy name Shusheng, was raised in the palace because his father had died in the service of the throne.

sentences.zh: 及長，襲爵廣宗公，起家左千牛。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he inherited the title Duke of Guangzong and began his career as Left Qianniu.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he inherited the title Duke of Guangzong and entered service as Left Qianniu.

sentences.zh: 美姿容，善騎射，工歌舞弦管。

translations.literal: He had handsome looks, was skilled at riding and archery, and was accomplished at singing, dancing, and string and wind music.
translations.idiomatic: He was handsome, skilled at riding and archery, and accomplished in song, dance, and string and wind music.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，周宣帝后樂平公主有女娥英，妙擇婚對，敕貴公子弟集弘聖宮者，日以百數。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, the Empress of Emperor Xuan of Zhou, Princess Leping, had a daughter Eying; she carefully chose a marriage match and ordered noble sons and younger brothers to gather at Hongsheng Palace by the hundreds each day.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaihuang, Princess Leping, empress of Emperor Xuan of Zhou, had a daughter named Eying; seeking a worthy match, she summoned noble youths to Hongsheng Palace by the hundreds each day.

sentences.zh: 公主選取敏，禮儀如尚帝女。

translations.literal: The princess selected Min; the rites were as for marrying an imperial daughter.
translations.idiomatic: The princess chose Min, and the wedding rites were conducted as for an imperial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 後將侍宴，公主謂敏曰：「我以天下與至尊，唯一女夫，當為汝求柱國。

translations.literal: Later, when he was about to attend a banquet, the princess said to Min: "I gave the empire to His Majesty—all that I have is one son-in-law; I shall get you the rank of Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: Before a banquet at court, the princess told Min, "I gave the empire to His Majesty; you are my only son-in-law, and I shall secure the rank of Pillar of State for you.

sentences.zh: 若授餘官，慎無謝。」

translations.literal: If they grant any other office, be careful not to thank them.
translations.idiomatic: If they grant any lesser office, be sure not to accept it.

sentences.zh: 及進見上，上親禦琵琶，遣敏歌舞，大悅，謂公主曰：「敏何官？」

translations.literal: When he went in to see the emperor, the emperor personally played the pipa and had Min sing and dance; greatly pleased, he asked the princess: "What office does Min hold?
translations.idiomatic: When Min was presented at court, the emperor himself played the pipa and had him sing and dance; greatly pleased, he asked the princess, "What rank does Min hold?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「一白丁耳。」

translations.literal: She replied: "Merely a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: She answered, "He is nothing but a commoner.

sentences.zh: 謂敏曰：「今授儀同。」

translations.literal: He said to Min: "I now grant you Pillar-of-State-equivalent rank.
translations.idiomatic: He said to Min, "I now grant you Pillar-of-State-equivalent rank.

sentences.zh: 敏不答。

translations.literal: Min did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Min made no reply.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「不滿爾意耶？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Not satisfied with your wish?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Not to your liking?

sentences.zh: 今授開府。」

translations.literal: I now grant you Opening-the-Fu rank.
translations.idiomatic: I now grant you Opening-the-Fu rank.

sentences.zh: 又不謝。

translations.literal: He still did not thank him.
translations.idiomatic: Min still did not thank him.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「公主有大功于我，我何得向其女婿惜官，今授卿柱國。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The princess rendered me great service—how could I be stingy with offices toward her son-in-law? I now grant you Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The princess rendered me great service—how could I begrudge her son-in-law an office? I now grant you Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 敏乃拜而蹈舞。

translations.literal: Min then bowed and danced in place.
translations.idiomatic: Min then bowed and danced in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 遂於坐發詔授柱國，以本官宿衛。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued on the spot granting Pillar of State, and he remained on palace guard duty in his existing post.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued on the spot granting Pillar of State, and he continued on palace guard duty in his existing post.

sentences.zh: 時或言敏一名洪兒，帝疑「洪」字當讖，嘗面告之，冀其引決。

translations.literal: At the time some said Min also had the name Hong'er; the emperor suspected the character "Hong" fulfilled a prophecy and once told him to his face, hoping he would take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Min also went by the name Hong'er; the emperor suspected the character "Hong" fulfilled a prophecy and once told him so to his face, hoping he would take his own life.

sentences.zh: 敏由是大懼，數與金才、善衡等屏人私語。

translations.literal: Min was thereby greatly afraid and often spoke privately with Jin Cai, Shanheng, and others with no one else present.
translations.idiomatic: Min was terrified and often met privately with Jin Cai, Shanheng, and others, speaking with no one else present.

sentences.zh: 宇文述知而奏之，竟與渾同誅。

translations.literal: Yuwen Shu learned of this and reported it; in the end he was executed together with Hun.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shu learned of this and reported it; in the end Min was executed together with Hun.

sentences.zh: 其妻宇文氏尋亦賜鴆而終。

translations.literal: His wife, of the Yuwen clan, was soon also granted poisoned wine and died.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, a Yuwen, was soon given poisoned wine and died.

sentences.zh: 賢弟遠。

translations.literal: Xian's younger brother Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's younger brother was Yuan.

sentences.zh: 遠字萬歲，幼有器局，嘗與群兒為戰鬥戲，指麾便有軍陣之法。

translations.literal: Yuan, courtesy name Wansui, as a child had capacity and vision; once when playing at battle with other boys, his directing already showed the methods of army formations.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, courtesy name Wansui, showed talent and breadth of mind even as a boy; once, playing at war with other children, his commands already displayed the logic of real battle formations.

sentences.zh: 郡守見而異之，召使更戲。

translations.literal: The prefect saw this and found it remarkable; he summoned them to perform again.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect saw this and was astonished; he summoned the boys to play again.

sentences.zh: 群兒散走，遠持杖叱之，復為向陣，意氣雄壯，殆甚於前。

translations.literal: The other boys scattered and fled; Yuan held a staff and shouted at them and again drew them into formation; his spirit was bold and stout, almost more than before.
translations.idiomatic: The other boys scattered, but Yuan seized a staff, shouted them back into line, and re-formed the ranks with a boldness that surpassed what had come before.

sentences.zh: 郡守曰：「此小兒必為將帥，非常人也。」

translations.literal: The prefect said: "This boy will surely become a general—he is no ordinary person."
translations.idiomatic: The prefect said, "This boy will surely become a commander—he is no ordinary child."

sentences.zh: 及長，涉獵書傳。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he read widely in books and records.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, he read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 魏正光末，天下鼎沸，敕勒賊胡琮侵逼原州。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenguang era of Wei, the realm boiled; the Tiele bandit Hu Cong attempted to invade Yuan province.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenguang era, the realm was in turmoil; the Tiele bandit Hu Cong pressed upon Yuan province.

sentences.zh: 遠昆季率勵鄉人，欲圖拒守，而眾情頗有異同。

translations.literal: Yuan and his brothers led and encouraged the local people to plan resistance and defense, but popular sentiment was much divided.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan and his brothers rallied the local people to resist and hold out, but opinion among them was sharply divided.

sentences.zh: 遠乃按劍喻以節義，因曰：「有異議者，請斬之。」

translations.literal: Yuan then drew his sword and reasoned with them on loyalty and righteousness, saying: "Whoever disagrees, step forward and be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan drew his sword and appealed to their sense of duty, saying, "Whoever disagrees, step forward and be beheaded.

sentences.zh: 眾懼，乃聽命，相與盟歃，深壁自守。

translations.literal: The crowd was afraid and then obeyed; they joined in oath by drinking blood and fortified the walls for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the people submitted; they swore a blood oath together and fortified the walls to hold out.

sentences.zh: 無援，城隱，其徒多被害，唯遠兄弟並為人所匿，得免。

translations.literal: With no relief, the city fell; many of their followers were killed—only Yuan and his brothers were hidden by others and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: With no relief coming, the city fell; many of their followers were killed, but Yuan and his brothers were hidden by others and escaped.

sentences.zh: 遠乃使賢晦跡和光，潛身間行，入朝求援。

translations.literal: Yuan then had Xian conceal himself and keep a low profile, traveling secretly by unfrequented routes to enter the court and seek aid.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan then sent Xian to keep a low profile and travel by hidden routes to the capital to seek aid.

sentences.zh: 魏朝嘉之，授武騎常侍，俄轉別將。

translations.literal: The Wei court commended this and granted him Regular Palace Cavalry; soon he was transferred to Separate General.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei court commended this and made him Regular Palace Cavalry Attendant; soon he was transferred to Separate General.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃天光西伐，配遠精兵為鄉導。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Tianguang marched west on campaign, Yuan was assigned elite troops as local guide.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Tianguang marched west, Yuan was assigned elite troops to serve as local guide.

sentences.zh: 天光欽遠才望，除為長城郡守。

translations.literal: Tianguang admired Yuan's talent and reputation and appointed him Prefect of Changcheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang admired Yuan's talent and reputation and appointed him Prefect of Changcheng.

sentences.zh: 後以應侯莫陳崇功。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted for responding to Hou Mo Chen Chong's merit.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted for his service under Hou Mo Chen Chong.

sentences.zh: 遷高平郡守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Prefect of Gaoping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Prefect of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 周文見面悅之，令居麾下。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai was pleased when he met him face to face and had him remain under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai was pleased when he met him and kept him in his own service.

sentences.zh: 及魏孝武西遷，封安定縣伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, he was enfeoffed as Earl of Anding county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Yuan was enfeoffed as Earl of Anding.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝嗣位之始，思享遐年，以遠字可嘉，令扶帝升殿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wen of Wei's accession, wishing to enjoy long years, because Yuan's courtesy name was auspicious, he had Yuan assist the emperor in ascending the hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Wen of Wei's reign, wishing long life for himself, he found Yuan's courtesy name auspicious and had Yuan assist him in ascending the hall.

sentences.zh: 進爵為公，仍領左右。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Duke and still led the Left and Right.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to duke and continued to lead the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 從征竇泰，復弘農，並有殊勳。

translations.literal: He followed in campaigns against Dou Tai and in recapturing Hongnong, both times with outstanding merit.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaigns against Dou Tai and the recapture of Hongnong, distinguishing himself in both.

sentences.zh: 授都督、原州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commander and Governor of Yuan province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Commander and Governor of Yuan province.

sentences.zh: 周文謂遠曰：「孤有卿，若身之有臂。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai said to Yuan: "Alone I have you, as the body has its arms.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai said to Yuan, "With you at my side I am as a body with arms.

sentences.zh: 本州之榮，乃私事爾。」

translations.literal: The glory of one's home province is a private matter.
translations.idiomatic: The honor of governing one's home province is a private matter.

sentences.zh: 遂令遠兄賢代行州事。

translations.literal: He then had Yuan's elder brother Xian administer provincial affairs in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore had Yuan's elder brother Xian administer the province in his place.

sentences.zh: 沙苑之役，遠功居最，進爵陽平郡公。

translations.literal: At the Battle of Shaye, Yuan's merit ranked highest; he was advanced to Duke of Yangping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Shaye Yuan's merit ranked first, and he was advanced to Duke of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 尋除大丞相府司馬，參軍國機務。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Chief of Staff of the Grand Chancellor's Office and participated in state military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Chief of Staff of the Grand Chancellor's Office and took part in the state's military affairs.

sentences.zh: 時河東初復，人情未安。

translations.literal: At that time Hedong had just been recovered, and the people's hearts were not yet settled.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong had only recently been recovered, and the people were still unsettled.

sentences.zh: 周文以河東為國之要領，乃授河東郡守。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai regarded Hedong as a vital artery of the state and therefore appointed him Prefect of Hedong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai considered Hedong a vital artery of the realm and appointed Li Yuan Prefect of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 遠敦獎風俗，勸課農桑，肅遏奸非，兼修守之備。

translations.literal: Li Yuan earnestly encouraged custom, urged farming and mulberry, sternly checked villainy and wrongdoing, and at the same time made preparations for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan worked to restore local custom, urged agriculture and sericulture, sternly suppressed crime, and at the same time readied the defenses.

sentences.zh: 曾未期月，百姓懷之。

translations.literal: Before a full month had passed, the common people were attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: In less than a month the people had come to trust him.

sentences.zh: 周文降書勞問。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai issued an imperial letter commending and inquiring after him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai sent an edict of commendation and inquiry.

sentences.zh: 徵為侍中，遷太子少師。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Palace Attendant and transferred to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Palace Attendant and appointed Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 東魏北豫州刺史高仲密請舉州來附，周文以仲密所據遼遠，難為應接。

translations.literal: Gao Zhongmi, Governor of Beiyu province of Eastern Wei, asked to bring his entire province over in submission; Yuwen Tai thought the place Zhongmi held was remote and far, and hard to support.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhongmi, Governor of Beiyu in Eastern Wei, offered to surrender his entire province; Yuwen Tai judged the territory too distant for easy relief.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆憚此行。

translations.literal: All the generals dreaded this expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Every general shrank from the mission.

sentences.zh: 遠曰：「北豫遠在賊境，高歡又屯兵河陽，常理而論，實難救援。

translations.literal: Li Yuan said: "Beiyu lies far in enemy territory, and Gao Huan also has troops stationed at Heyang; by ordinary reasoning, rescue would truly be difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan said, "Beiyu lies deep in enemy territory, and Gao Huan holds Heyang with his army—by ordinary reckoning relief would be all but impossible.

sentences.zh: 但不入獸穴，不得獸子，若以奇兵出其不意，事或可濟。

translations.literal: Yet if one does not enter the beast's den, one cannot obtain the beast's cubs; if one sends a surprise force where they do not expect it, the affair might yet succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet one must enter the tiger's den to take the cubs—if we strike with a surprise force where they do not expect us, the enterprise may yet succeed.

sentences.zh: 脫有利鈍，故是兵家之常。

translations.literal: If there is success or setback, that is simply the way of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gain and loss alike are the common lot of war.

sentences.zh: 如其顧望不行，便無克定之日。」

translations.literal: If one hangs back and does not go, there will never be a day of conquest and pacification.
translations.idiomatic: If we hang back and refuse to go, there will never be a day of victory.

sentences.zh: 周文喜曰：「李萬歲所言，差強人意。」

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai was pleased and said: "What Li Yuan Wansui has said barely satisfies one's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai was pleased and said, "Li Yuan Wansui's words are most heartening.

sentences.zh: 乃授行台尚書，前驅東出。

translations.literal: He then appointed him Mobile-Directorate Director and vanguard marching east.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Li Yuan Director of the Mobile Directorate and sent him ahead as vanguard marching east.

sentences.zh: 周文率大軍繼進。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai led the great army in continued advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai followed with the main army.

sentences.zh: 遠乃潛師而往，拔仲密以歸。

translations.literal: Li Yuan then moved his army secretly and brought Zhongmi out in rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan marched in secret and brought Zhongmi safely out.

sentences.zh: 仍從周文戰於芒山，時大軍不利，遠獨整所部為殿。

translations.literal: He still followed Yuwen Tai in battle at Mount Mang; at that time the great army was at a disadvantage, and Li Yuan alone ordered his command as rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: He fought with Yuwen Tai at Mount Mang; when the main army faltered, Li Yuan alone kept his troops in order as rearguard.

sentences.zh: 尋授都督義州弘農等二十一郡諸軍事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Commander-in-Chief over military affairs of twenty-one commanderies including Yizhou and Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Commander-in-Chief over military affairs in twenty-one commanderies including Yizhou and Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 遠善撫馭，有幹略，戰守之備，無不精銳。

translations.literal: Li Yuan was good at comforting and controlling; he had capacity and strategy; preparations for battle and defense—none were not sharp and keen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan governed with skill and had both talent and resolution; every measure for offense and defense was honed to a keen edge.

sentences.zh: 每厚撫境外之人，使為間諜，敵中動靜，必先知之。

translations.literal: Each time he treated persons beyond the border generously and had them serve as spies; movements within the enemy camp he always knew beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: He generously cultivated people beyond the border as spies, so he always knew the enemy's movements before they happened.

sentences.zh: 至有事泄被誅，亦不以為悔。

translations.literal: Even when affairs were leaked and spies were executed, he did not regard it as regret.
translations.idiomatic: Even when informants were exposed and executed, he never regretted the method.

sentences.zh: 嘗獵於莎柵，見石于叢薄中，以為伏兔，射之，鏃入寸餘，視之乃石。

translations.literal: Once while hunting at Shazha he saw a stone in the thickets, took it for a crouching rabbit, shot it, and the arrowhead sank more than an inch; looking at it, it was stone.
translations.idiomatic: Once while hunting at Shazha he spotted something in the brush, took it for a hiding rabbit, and shot it—the arrowhead sank more than an inch into what proved to be stone.

sentences.zh: 周文聞面異之，賜書曰：「昔李將軍親有此事，公今復爾，可謂世載其德矣。」

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai heard of it and was amazed face to face; he bestowed a letter saying: "Formerly General Li himself had this affair; you now repeat it—one may say virtue is borne through generations.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai heard of it and marveled; he wrote, "Long ago General Li did the same, and you have done it again—truly virtue runs in the blood.

sentences.zh: 東魏將段孝先趣宜陽，以送糧為名，實有窺窬之意。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei general Duan Xiaoxian hastened to Yiyang; in the name of delivering grain, in fact he had designs of encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Wei general Duan Xiaoxian marched on Yiyang under the pretext of delivering supplies, but in truth meant to seize it.

sentences.zh: 遠密知其計，遣兵襲破之。

translations.literal: Li Yuan secretly knew his plan and sent troops to strike and defeat him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan learned his plan in secret and sent troops to surprise and rout him.

sentences.zh: 孝先遁走。

translations.literal: Xiaoxian fled in escape.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxian fled.

sentences.zh: 周文賜所乘主金帶床帳衣被等，並彩二千匹，拜大將軍。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai bestowed the gold belt, bed, curtains, clothing, and bedding of his own mount, together with two thousand bolts of colored silk, and appointed him Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai gave him the gold belt, bed, hangings, clothing, and bedding from his own carriage, two thousand bolts of colored silk, and the rank of Grand General.

sentences.zh: 頃之，除尚書左僕射，固辭。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Left Vice-Director of the Masters of Writing; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was named Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, but firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 周文不許，遠不得已，方拜職。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai would not allow it; Li Yuan had no choice and only then accepted the office.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai would not hear of it; Li Yuan had no choice and at last accepted the post.

sentences.zh: 周文又以第十一子代王達令遠子之，其見親待如此。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai also had his eleventh son, Prince Dai Wang Da, take Li Yuan as mentor; such was the degree of his intimate favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai also had his eleventh son, Prince Dai, Wang Da, take Li Yuan as mentor—such was the depth of his trust and favor.

sentences.zh: 時周文嫡嗣未建，明居長，已有成德；

translations.literal: At that time Yuwen Tai's legitimate heir was not yet established; Ming as eldest already had mature virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai had not yet designated a legitimate heir; Ming, the eldest, already showed mature virtue;

sentences.zh: 孝閔處嫡，年尚幼沖。

translations.literal: Xiaomin was by position the legitimate son, but his years were still young and tender.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaomin was the legitimate son, but still very young.

sentences.zh: 乃謂群公曰：「孤欲立子以嫡，恐大司馬有疑。」

translations.literal: He then said to the assembled lords: "I wish to establish the son by legitimacy of birth; I fear the Grand Marshal may harbor doubts.
translations.idiomatic: He told the assembled lords, "I wish to install the legitimate son as heir, but I fear the Grand Marshal may object.

sentences.zh: 大司馬即獨孤信，明帝敬後父也。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal was Dugu Xin, father of Empress Jing of Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal was Dugu Xin, father of Emperor Ming's empress.

sentences.zh: 眾未有答。

translations.literal: The assembly had no reply yet.
translations.idiomatic: No one answered.

sentences.zh: 遠曰：「立子以嫡不以長，略陽公為嗣，公何疑焉？

translations.literal: Li Yuan said: "One establishes the son by legitimacy of birth, not by seniority; the Duke of Lueyang should be heir—what doubt have you?
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan said, "The heir is chosen by legitimacy, not age—the Duke of Lueyang is the rightful successor. Why hesitate?

sentences.zh: 若以人為嫌，請即斬信。」

translations.literal: If you take a person as the obstacle, I ask to behead Xin immediately.
translations.idiomatic: If a man stands in the way, I shall cut down Xin here and now.

sentences.zh: 便起拔劍。

translations.literal: He thereupon rose and drew his sword.
translations.idiomatic: He rose and drew his sword.

sentences.zh: 周文亦起曰：「何事至此！」

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai also rose and said: "Why has it come to this!
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai rose as well and cried, "What need is there for this!

sentences.zh: 信又自陳產，遠乃止。

translations.literal: Xin again declared himself in labor; Li Yuan then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Xin pleaded that his daughter was in labor, and Li Yuan desisted.

sentences.zh: 於是群公並從遠議。

translations.literal: Thereupon the assembled lords all followed Li Yuan's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the lords all sided with Li Yuan.

sentences.zh: 遠出外，拜謝信曰：「臨大事不得不爾。」

translations.literal: Li Yuan went outside and bowed in apology to Xin, saying: "Facing a great affair, one cannot but act thus.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan went out and bowed to Xin in apology, saying, "In so grave a matter I had no choice.

sentences.zh: 信亦謝遠曰：「今日賴公決此大議。」

translations.literal: Xin also apologized to Li Yuan, saying: "Today we rely on you, Lord, to decide this great matter.
translations.idiomatic: Xin in turn apologized to Li Yuan, saying, "Today we owe this great decision to you.

sentences.zh: 六官建，授小司寇。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed Minor Director of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were created, he was made Minor Director of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐祚，進位柱國大將軍，復鎮弘農。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, Li Yuan was advanced to Duke of the State and Grand General and again garrisoned Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Li Yuan was promoted to Duke of the State and Grand General and again garrisoned Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 遠子植，文帝時已為相府司錄，參掌朝政。

translations.literal: Li Yuan's son Zhi, in Emperor Wen's time, had already been Chief Recorder of the Chancellor's Office and participated in directing court policy.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan's son Zhi had already served in Emperor Wen's time as Chief Recorder of the Chancellor's Office and helped run the government.

sentences.zh: 及晉公護執權，密欲誅護，頗泄，護乃出植為梁州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Jin, Hu, seized power, he secretly wished to kill Hu; the plot leaked somewhat, and Hu then sent Zhi out as Governor of Liang province.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Hu seized power as Duke of Jin, Zhi secretly plotted to kill him; the plot leaked, and Hu posted Zhi to Governor of Liang.

sentences.zh: 尋而廢帝，召遠及植還朝。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor was deposed, and Li Yuan and Zhi were summoned back to court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor was deposed, and Li Yuan and Zhi were recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 遠恐有變，沉吟良久，乃曰：「大丈夫寧為忠鬼，安能作叛臣乎！」

translations.literal: Li Yuan feared trouble and brooded for a long while, then said: "A great man would rather be a loyal ghost—how could he become a rebel minister!
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan feared treachery and brooded a long while, then said, "A true man would rather die a loyal ghost than live a rebel!

sentences.zh: 遂就征，至京師。

translations.literal: He thereupon obeyed the summons and reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He obeyed the summons and went to the capital.

sentences.zh: 護以遠功名素重，猶欲全宥之，謂曰：「公兒遂有異謀，可早為之所。」

translations.literal: Hu, because Li Yuan's merit and reputation had always been weighty, still wished to preserve and pardon him, saying: "Your son indeed had a different plot—you should deal with it early.
translations.idiomatic: Because Li Yuan's reputation was great, Hu still meant to spare him and said, "Your son has indeed plotted rebellion—you had best deal with him yourself.

sentences.zh: 乃以植付遠。

translations.literal: He then handed Zhi over to Li Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He handed Zhi over to Li Yuan.

sentences.zh: 遠素愛植，植又有口辯，雲初無此謀。

translations.literal: Li Yuan had always loved Zhi; Zhi also had eloquence in speech and declared at first that there had been no such plot.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan had always loved Zhi, and Zhi was glib of tongue and at first denied any such plot.

sentences.zh: 遠信之，詰朝將植謁護。

translations.literal: Li Yuan believed him; the next morning he was about to bring Zhi to visit Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan believed him, and the next morning took Zhi to call on Hu.

sentences.zh: 護謂植已死，乃曰：「陽平公何意自來？」

translations.literal: Hu thought Zhi was already dead and therefore said: "Lord Duke of Yangping, what do you mean by coming yourself?
translations.idiomatic: Hu had thought Zhi already dead and said, "Duke of Yangping, why have you come in person?

sentences.zh: 左右云：「植亦在門外。」

translations.literal: Those at his side said: "Zhi is also at the gate outside.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants said, "Zhi is at the gate as well.

sentences.zh: 護大怒曰：「陽平公不信我矣！」

translations.literal: Hu was greatly angered and said: "Lord Duke of Yangping no longer trusts me!
translations.idiomatic: Hu flew into a rage and cried, "The Duke of Yangping no longer trusts me!

sentences.zh: 召入，命遠同坐，令帝與植相質於遠前。

translations.literal: He summoned them in, ordered Li Yuan to sit together with him, and had the emperor and Zhi confront each other before Li Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He had them brought in, seated Li Yuan beside him, and made the emperor and Zhi confront each other before Li Yuan.

sentences.zh: 植辭窮，謂帝曰：「本為此謀，欲安社稷，利至尊耳。

translations.literal: Zhi's words were exhausted; he said to the emperor: "Originally this plot was made wishing to settle the altars of soil and grain and benefit Your Majesty alone.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi could say no more and told the emperor, "We plotted only to secure the realm and serve Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 今日至此，何事云云。」

translations.literal: Today it has come to this—what need for all this talk.
translations.idiomatic: And now it has come to this—what more is there to say?

sentences.zh: 遠聞之，自投於床，曰：「若爾，誠合萬死。」

translations.literal: Li Yuan heard it and threw himself upon the bed, saying: "If so, truly death ten thousand times over would be fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan heard this and fell upon the bed, crying, "If that is so, I deserve to die ten thousand deaths.

sentences.zh: 於是護乃害植，並逼遠自殺。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hu then killed Zhi and also compelled Li Yuan to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hu then killed Zhi and forced Li Yuan to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 建德元年，晉公護誅，贈本官，加太保，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiande, when the Duke of Jin Hu was executed, posthumous honors restored his former office, added Grand Guardian, posthumous title Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiande, after Yuwen Hu was executed, Li Yuan was posthumously restored to his former rank with the added title Grand Guardian and the posthumous name Loyal.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，追贈上柱國，改諡曰懷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang of Sui, he was further posthumously enfeoffed Duke of the Upper State and his posthumous title was changed to Pondering.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang era of Sui, he was further enfeoffed as Duke of the Upper State and his posthumous name was changed to Pondering.

sentences.zh: 植及諸弟並加諡。

translations.literal: Zhi and the various younger brothers all received added posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and Li Yuan's other sons all received posthumous titles as well.

sentences.zh: 威字安人，又改襲遠爵陽平郡公，加上開府。

translations.literal: Wei, courtesy name Anren, again changed to inherit Li Yuan's title Duke of Yangping commandery and was added Opening the Government.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, courtesy name Anren, eventually inherited Li Yuan's title as Duke of Yangping and was given the rank Opening the Government.

sentences.zh: 大象末，地至柱國，封公。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang, his rank reached Duke of the State and he was enfeoffed as Duke.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Daxiang era he had risen to Duke of the State and been enfeoffed as duke.

sentences.zh: 賢弟穆，字顯慶，少明敏有度量。

translations.literal: Xian's younger brother Mu, courtesy name Xianqing, in youth was bright, keen, and had measure.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's younger brother Li Mu, courtesy name Xianqing, was clever and far-sighted from youth.

sentences.zh: 文帝入關，便給事左右，深被親遇。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen entered the Pass, he immediately served in attendance at Left and Right and was deeply treated with intimate favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen entered the Pass, Li Mu entered his personal service and enjoyed his deep favor.

sentences.zh: 穆亦小心謹肅，未嘗懈怠。

translations.literal: Mu also was careful, respectful, and solemn, never slackening.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu was careful and reverent in his duties and never slackened.

sentences.zh: 及侯莫陳悅害賀拔岳，周文自夏州赴難，而悅黨史歸據原州，猶為悅守。

translations.literal: When Hou Mo Chen Yue killed Heba Yue, Yuwen Tai from Xia province rushed to the rescue, while Yue's partisan Shi Gui held Yuan province and still defended it for Yue.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Mo Chen Yue killed Heba Yue, Yuwen Tai marched from Xia province to the rescue; Yue's follower Shi Gui still held Yuan province for him.

sentences.zh: 周文令侯莫陳崇襲之，穆時先在城中，與兄賢、遠應崇，遂禽歸。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai ordered Hou Mo Chen Chong to strike him; Mu was then already in the city beforehand and with his elder brothers Xian and Li Yuan responded to Chong, then captured Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai sent Hou Mo Chen Chong against him; Li Mu was already in the city and, with his brothers Xian and Li Yuan, supported Chong and captured Shi Gui.

sentences.zh: 以功授都督。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed Commander.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was made Commander.

sentences.zh: 從迎魏孝武，封永平縣子。

translations.literal: He followed in welcoming Emperor Xiaowu of Wei and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Yongping county.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in welcoming Emperor Xiaowu of Wei and was enfeoffed Viscount of Yongping.

sentences.zh: 又領鄉兵。

translations.literal: He also led native troops.
translations.idiomatic: He also commanded local militia.

sentences.zh: 禽竇泰，復弘農，並有戰功。

translations.literal: Capturing Dou Tai and recapturing Hongnong—both had military merit.
