translations.idiomatic: He captured Dou Tai and helped retake Hongnong, distinguishing himself in both campaigns.

sentences.zh: 沙苑之捷，穆言：「歡今日已喪膽矣，請速逐之，則歡可禽也。」

translations.literal: At the victory of Shaye, Mu said: "Huan today has already lost his gall; I ask to pursue him quickly, then Huan can be captured.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory at Shaye, Li Mu said, "Gao Huan has lost his nerve today—pursue him at once and he can be taken.

sentences.zh: 周文不聽。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai would not hear it.

sentences.zh: 論前後功，進爵國公。

translations.literal: Weighing merit before and after, he was advanced to Duke of the State.
translations.idiomatic: Accounting for his merits overall, he was advanced to Duke of the State.

sentences.zh: 芒山之戰，周文馬中流矢，驚逸墜地。

translations.literal: In the battle of Mount Mang, Yuwen Tai's horse was struck by a flying arrow in mid-course, startled and bolted, and he fell to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Mang Yuwen Tai's horse was struck by an arrow, bolted in panic, and threw him to the ground.

sentences.zh: 敵人追及，左右皆散。

translations.literal: The enemy caught up; those left and right all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy closed in, and his attendants scattered.

sentences.zh: 穆下馬，以策擊周文背，因大罵曰：「籠陳軍士，爾曹主何在？

translations.literal: Mu dismounted, struck Yuwen Tai's back with a riding crop, and therefore loudly cursed, saying: "Longchen soldiers—where is your master?
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu dismounted, struck Yuwen Tai's back with his whip, and shouted abuse: "Soldiers of Longchen—where is your commander?

sentences.zh: 爾獨住此！」

translations.literal: You alone stay here!
translations.idiomatic: And you dawdle here alone!

sentences.zh: 敵人見其輕侮，不疑是貴人，遂舍而過。

translations.literal: The enemy saw his contempt and did not suspect he was a noble, then let go and passed by.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy, seeing him treated with contempt, never guessed he was a person of rank and passed on.

sentences.zh: 穆以馬授周文，遂俱逸。

translations.literal: Mu gave his horse to Yuwen Tai and then both escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu gave Yuwen Tai his horse, and both escaped together.

sentences.zh: 是日微穆，周文已不濟矣。

translations.literal: That day, but for Mu, Yuwen Tai would already have been beyond saving.
translations.idiomatic: But for Li Mu that day, Yuwen Tai would not have survived.

sentences.zh: 既而與穆相對而泣，自是恩盼更隆。

translations.literal: Before long he and Mu faced each other and wept; from then on gracious favor was even loftier.
translations.idiomatic: He and Li Mu then wept face to face, and from that day his favor toward Mu only deepened.

sentences.zh: 顧左右曰：「成我事者，其此人乎！」

translations.literal: Turning to left and right he said: "The one who accomplished my affairs—is it not this man!
translations.idiomatic: He turned to his attendants and said, "The man who saved me—is this not he!

sentences.zh: 擢授武衛將軍、儀同三司，進封安武郡公。

translations.literal: He was promoted and appointed General of the Martial Guard, Equal in Glory to the Three Excellencies, and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Anwu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu was promoted to General of the Martial Guard, given ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, and advanced to Duke of Anwu.

sentences.zh: 前後賞賜，不可勝計。

translations.literal: Rewards before and after could not be fully counted.
translations.idiomatic: The rewards that followed were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 周文歎其忠節，曰：「人所貴唯命，穆遂輕命濟孤，爵位玉帛，未足為報。」

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai sighed at his loyalty and constancy, saying: "What men value is life alone; Mu then lightly valued life to save me alone—rank, title, and silks are not enough to repay him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai marveled at his loyalty and said, "Life is what men hold most dear—yet Mu risked his own to save mine. Rank and silk are not reward enough.

sentences.zh: 乃特賜鐵券，恕以十死。

translations.literal: He then specially bestowed an iron certificate, pardoning ten deaths.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore granted him an iron tally forgiving ten capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、侍中。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Cavalry General-in-Chief, Opening the Government with Equal Glory to the Three Excellencies, and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Cavalry General-in-Chief, given the rank Opening the Government with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies, and made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 初，芒山之敗，穆授周文炍馬，後中廄此色者，悉以賜之。

translations.literal: At first, at the defeat of Mount Mang, Mu gave Yuwen Tai a piebald horse; afterward, piebald horses in the central stables of this color were all given to him.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Mount Mang, Li Mu had given Yuwen Tai a piebald horse; afterward every piebald in the imperial stud was given to him.

sentences.zh: 又賜穆嗣子惇安樂郡公，姊一人為郡君，自余姊妹並為縣君，兄弟子侄及緦麻已上親並舅氏皆沾厚賜。

translations.literal: He also enfeoffed Mu's heir Dun as Duke of Anle commandery; one elder sister as Commandery Lady; the remaining sisters all as County Ladies; brothers', sons', nephews', and relatives within the mourning-grade of fine hemp and above, together with maternal uncles' families, all received thick gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He also enfeoffed Li Mu's heir Dun as Duke of Anle, made one sister a Commandery Lady and the rest County Ladies, and showered rich gifts on brothers, sons, nephews, kin within the fifth mourning degree, and the maternal clan alike.

sentences.zh: 其褒崇如此。

translations.literal: His encomium and exaltation were to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the honor lavished upon him.

sentences.zh: 從解玉壁圍，拜安定國中尉。

translations.literal: He followed in lifting the siege of Yubi and was appointed Captain of the State of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in raising the siege of Yubi and was made Captain of the State of Anding.

sentences.zh: 曆同州刺史、太僕卿。

translations.literal: He successively served as Governor of Tong province and Grand Steward.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Governor of Tong province and Grand Steward.

sentences.zh: 從于謹平江陵，以功別封一子長城縣侯。

translations.literal: He followed Yu Jin in pacifying Jiangling and, for merit, separately enfeoffed one son as Marquis of Changcheng county.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Yu Jin in the pacification of Jiangling and, for his merit, had one son separately enfeoffed as Marquis of Changcheng.

sentences.zh: 尋進位大將軍，賜姓拓拔氏。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Grand General and granted the surname Tabgach.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Grand General and granted the surname Tabgach.

sentences.zh: 又擊曲沔蠻破之。

translations.literal: Again he attacked the Qu-Mian barbarians and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He again attacked the Qu-Mian tribes and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 俄除原州刺史，拜世子惇為儀同三司，以賢子為平高郡守，遠子為平高縣令，並加鼓吹。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Governor of Yuan province; his heir Dun was appointed Honorary Three Excellencies Associate; Xian's son was made Prefect of Pinggao commandery, Yuan's son Prefect of Pinggao county—all were granted ceremonial music.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Mu was made Governor of Yuan province. His heir Dun was given the rank of Honorary Three Excellencies Associate; Li Xian's son was appointed Prefect of Pinggao, and Li Yuan's son Prefect of Pinggao county—all with ceremonial retinue music.

sentences.zh: 穆自以叔侄一家三人皆牧宰鄉里，恩遇過隆，固辭不拜。

translations.literal: Mu himself considered that uncle and nephew, one family with three men all governing their home region—the favor was excessive—and firmly declined to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu felt that having three men of one uncle-nephew household all governing their native region was excessive favor, and firmly declined the appointments.

sentences.zh: 周文不許。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 後人為雍州刺史，兼小塚宰。

translations.literal: Afterward he was made Governor of Yong province and concurrently Lesser Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Governor of Yong province and concurrently made Lesser Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，又封一子為升遷縣伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, one son was again enfeoffed as Earl of Shengqian county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, Li Mu had another son enfeoffed as Earl of Shengqian.

sentences.zh: 穆請回授賢子孝軌，許之。

translations.literal: Mu requested that it be transferred back and granted to Xian's son Xiaogui; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu asked that the title be transferred to Li Xian's son Xiaogui, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 及兄子植謀害宇文護被誅，穆亦坐除名。

translations.literal: When his elder brother's son Zhi plotted to harm Yuwen Hu and was executed, Mu also by association was stripped of name and rank.
translations.idiomatic: When his nephew Li Zhi plotted against Yuwen Hu and was executed, Li Mu was also struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 先是穆知植非保家主，每勸遠除之，遠不能用。

translations.literal: Earlier Mu had known Zhi was not one to preserve the family and repeatedly urged Yuan to remove him; Yuan could not act on it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu had long known that Li Zhi was no keeper of the family line and repeatedly urged Li Yuan to get rid of him, but Li Yuan would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及遠臨刑，泣謂穆曰：「顯慶，吾不用汝言以至此，將奈何！」

translations.literal: When Yuan faced execution, weeping he said to Mu: "Xianqing, by not heeding your words I have come to this—what is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yuan faced execution, he wept and said to Li Mu, "Xianqing, I did not listen to you and have come to this—what can I do now?

sentences.zh: 穆以此獲免，及其子弟亦免官。

translations.literal: Mu for this reason was spared execution, and his sons and younger brothers were also dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu was spared on this account, and his sons and younger brothers were merely dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 時植弟基當從坐戮，穆求以子惇、怡等代死，辭理酸切，聞者莫不動容。

translations.literal: At the time Zhi's younger brother Ji was due to be executed by association; Mu begged that his sons Dun, Yi, and others die in his stead—the reasoning bitter and piercing; all who heard were moved.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi's younger brother Ji was bound for execution as an accomplice; Li Mu begged that his sons Dun and Yi die in Ji's place. His plea was wrenching, and all who heard were moved.

sentences.zh: 護矜之，遂特免基死。

translations.literal: Hu took pity on him and specially spared Ji from death.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu was moved and specially spared Ji.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，拜驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、大都督，復爵安武郡公，拜直州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, he was appointed General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Secretary with Honorary Three Excellencies Associate, Great Commander; his title as Duke of Anwu commandery was restored, and he was appointed Governor of Zhi province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Li Mu was made General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Secretary with Honorary Three Excellencies Associate, and Great Commander; restored as Duke of Anwu and appointed Governor of Zhi province.

sentences.zh: 武成中，子弟免官爵者悉復之。

translations.literal: During the Wucheng era, sons and younger brothers who had lost office and ranks were all restored.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wucheng era, all sons and younger brothers who had lost rank were restored.

sentences.zh: 累遷大司空。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，進封申國公，舊爵回授一子。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe, he was advanced to Duke of Shen state; his old title was transferred back and granted to one son.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe 2, he was promoted to Duke of Shen; his former title was transferred to one of his sons.

sentences.zh: 建德元年，遷太保，尋出為原州總管。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiande, he was transferred to Grand Mentor; soon he went out as Commander of Yuan province.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiande 1 he was made Grand Mentor, and soon thereafter sent out as Commander of Yuan province.

sentences.zh: 四年，武帝東征，令穆別攻軹關及河北諸縣，並破之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Emperor Wu marched east; he ordered Mu separately to attack Zhiguan Pass and the counties of Hebei—all were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In year four, when Emperor Wu marched east, Li Mu was ordered to attack Zhiguan Pass and the Hebei counties separately, and overcame them all.

sentences.zh: 後以帝疾班師，棄而不守。

translations.literal: Later because the emperor fell ill the army withdrew; what had been taken was abandoned and not held.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill the army withdrew, and the gains were abandoned.

sentences.zh: 六年，進位上柱國，除并州總管。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was advanced to Preeminent Pillar of State and appointed Commander of Bing province.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he was promoted to Preeminent Pillar of State and made Commander of Bing province.

sentences.zh: 時東夏初平，人情尚擾，穆靖以鎮守，百姓懷之。

translations.literal: At the time eastern Xia had just been pacified and popular sentiment was still unsettled; Mu pacified through firm garrison, and the common people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Xia had only recently been pacified and the people were still unsettled; Li Mu kept order through steady garrison duty, and the people came to rely on him.

sentences.zh: 大象元年，加邑至九千戶，遷大左輔，總管如舊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daxiang, his fief households were increased to nine thousand; he was transferred to Grand Left Assistant, Commander as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Daxiang 1 his fief was increased to nine thousand households; he was made Grand Left Assistant while retaining his command.

sentences.zh: 二年，詔加太傅，仍總管。

translations.literal: In the second year, an edict added Grand Preceptor; he still held command.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made Grand Preceptor by edict, while continuing as commander.

sentences.zh: 及隋文作相，尉遲迥舉兵，遣使招穆，穆鎖其使，上其書。

translations.literal: When Sui Wen became Chancellor, Yu Chi Jiong raised troops and sent an envoy to recruit Mu; Mu locked up the envoy and submitted the letter.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became regent chancellor, Yuchi Jiong rose in arms and sent an envoy to win Li Mu over; Li Mu imprisoned the envoy and forwarded the letter to Yang Jian.

sentences.zh: 穆子士榮以穆所居天下精兵處，陰勸穆應之。

translations.literal: Mu's son Shirong, because the place where Mu dwelt was where the realm's finest troops were stationed, secretly urged Mu to respond to Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu's son Shirong, knowing that Bing province held the empire's finest troops, secretly urged his father to join Jiong.

sentences.zh: 穆弗聽，曰：「周德既衰，愚智共悉，天時若此，豈能違天？」

translations.literal: Mu would not listen and said: "Zhou's virtue has already declined; fool and wise alike know it; the times being thus, how can one go against Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu refused and said, "The Zhou dynasty's mandate is spent—everyone knows it. With the times as they are, how could I defy Heaven?

sentences.zh: 乃遣使謁隋文帝，並上十三環金帶，蓋天子服也，以微申其意。

translations.literal: He then sent an envoy to call on Emperor Wen of Sui and also submitted a thirteen-ring gold belt—the garb of a Son of Heaven—to faintly convey his meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent an envoy to Yang Jian and presented a thirteen-ring gold belt—the badge of imperial rank—hinting at his intentions.

sentences.zh: 時迥子誼為朔州刺史，亦執送京師。

translations.literal: At the time Jiong's son Yi was Governor of Shuo province and was also seized and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jiong's son Yi, then Governor of Shuo province, was also captured and sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 迥今其署行台韓長業攻陷潞州，執刺史趙威，署城人郭子勝為刺史。

translations.literal: Jiong ordered his acting commissary Han Changye to attack and capture Lu province, seize Governor Zhao Wei, and appoint a townsman Guo Zisheng as governor.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong ordered his Acting Commissary Han Changye to take Lu province, capture Governor Zhao Wei, and install a local man, Guo Zisheng, as governor.

sentences.zh: 穆遣兵討獲子勝。

translations.literal: Mu sent troops to attack and captured Zisheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu sent troops, captured Guo Zisheng, and restored order.

sentences.zh: 文帝嘉之，以穆勞同破鄴城第一勳，加三轉，聽分授其二子榮、才及賢子孝軌。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen praised this; considering Mu's merit equal to the first credit for breaking Ye city, he added three rank turns and permitted him to divide and grant them to his two sons Rong and Cai and to Xian's son Xiaogui.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian commended him; counting Li Mu's service equal to the foremost merit in the fall of Ye, he granted three extra rank steps and allowed Li Mu to divide them among his sons Rong and Cai and Li Xian's son Xiaogui.

sentences.zh: 榮及才並儀同大將軍，孝軌進開府儀同大將軍，又別封子雄為密國公。

translations.literal: Rong and Cai both became Honorary Generals; Xiaogui was advanced to Grand Secretary Honorary General; another son Xiong was separately enfeoffed Duke of Mi state.
translations.idiomatic: Rong and Cai were both made Honorary Generals; Xiaogui was promoted to Grand Secretary Honorary General; and another son, Xiong, was separately enfeoffed Duke of Mi.

sentences.zh: 穆又密表勸進。

translations.literal: Mu again submitted a secret memorial urging accession to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu also submitted a secret memorial urging Yang Jian to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 文帝既受禪，詔曰：「公既舊德，且又父党，敬惠來旨，便以今月十三日恭膺天命。」

translations.literal: After Emperor Wen had received the abdication, an edict said: "Lord, you have old virtue and are moreover of my father's generation; reverently accepting your gracious message, on the thirteenth of this month I humbly received Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Jian accepted the abdication, he issued an edict: "You are a man of old merit and of my father's generation. Honoring your counsel, on the thirteenth of this month I humbly took Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 俄而穆來朝，文帝降座禮之。

translations.literal: Soon Mu came to court; Emperor Wen descended from his seat to salute him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Mu came to court, and Yang Jian stepped down from the throne to receive him with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 拜太師，贊拜不名，真食成安縣三千戶。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Preceptor; at congratulatory bows his name was not spoken; he received in actuality the revenue of three thousand households of Chengan county.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu was made Grand Preceptor, granted the privilege of being addressed without his name at court, and given three thousand tax-paying households in Chengan county.

sentences.zh: 穆子孫雖在繈褓，悉拜儀同，其一門執象笏者百餘人，貴盛當時無比。

translations.literal: Mu's sons and grandsons, though still in swaddling clothes, were all appointed Honorary Associates; in one household over a hundred held ivory court tablets—nobility and splendor unmatched in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Even Li Mu's infant descendants were given Honorary Associate rank; more than a hundred in his clan carried ivory court tablets—none in the age matched their splendor.

sentences.zh: 穆上表乞骸骨，詔曰：「公年既耆舊，筋力難煩，今勒所司敬蠲朝集。

translations.literal: Mu submitted a memorial begging to retire on account of old bones; an edict said: "Lord, your years are already venerable and your sinews and strength are hard to trouble; henceforth I charge the offices reverently to exempt you from court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu asked leave to retire; the edict replied, "You are aged and your strength is not what it was. Henceforth the offices shall exempt you from the burden of court attendance.

sentences.zh: 如有大事，須共謀謨，別遣侍臣，就第詢訪。」

translations.literal: If there are great affairs, we must deliberate together—I shall separately send attendant ministers to your residence to inquire and consult.
translations.idiomatic: On great matters we shall still consult you; I shall send ministers to your home to seek your counsel.

sentences.zh: 時太史奏當有移都事，帝以初受命，甚難之。

translations.literal: At the time the Grand Astrologer memorialized that there should be a move of the capital; the emperor, having just received the mandate, found it very difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Astrologer then reported that the capital should be moved; the emperor, newly enthroned, was deeply reluctant.

sentences.zh: 穆乃上表極言宜移都之便。

translations.literal: Mu then submitted a memorial vigorously stating the convenience of moving the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu submitted a memorial strongly urging the advantages of moving the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝素嫌台城制度迮小，又宮內多鬼妖。

translations.literal: The emperor had long disliked that the capital city Taicheng's construction was cramped, and moreover within the palace there were many ghostly prodigies.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian had long disliked the cramped layout of Taicheng, and the palace was said to be haunted.

sentences.zh: 蘇威嘗勸遷，上不納，遇太史奏狀，意乃惑之。

translations.literal: Su Wei had once urged relocation; the emperor did not accept it; encountering the Grand Astrologer's memorial, his mind then was unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei had urged relocation before without success; the astrologer's report now made him waver.

sentences.zh: 至是省穆表，帝曰：「天道聰明，已有征應，太師人望，復抗此請，則可矣。」

translations.literal: At this he examined Mu's memorial; the emperor said: "Heaven's way is discerning—there are already signs and responses; the Grand Preceptor's public esteem again presses this request—then it will do.
translations.idiomatic: When he read Li Mu's memorial, the emperor said, "Heaven has already given its sign, and the Grand Preceptor—whom all respect—now urges this as well. It is settled.

sentences.zh: 遂之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went.
translations.idiomatic: And so the capital was moved.

sentences.zh: 長子惇字士獻。

translations.literal: The eldest son Dun, courtesy name Shixian.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Dun, courtesy name Shixian.

sentences.zh: 周文帝令功臣長子並與略陽公遊處，惇於輩流中特被引接，每有遐方服玩珍奇，無不班賜。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou ordered that eldest sons of meritorious ministers all keep company with the Duke of Lueyang; among his peers Dun was especially received and welcomed—whenever there were exotic garments, curios, and rarities from distant regions, none failed to be distributed and bestowed to him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou had the eldest sons of his great ministers keep company with the Duke of Lueyang; among them Dun was singled out for special favor, and every exotic treasure from afar was shared with him.

sentences.zh: 封安樂郡公，位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、鳳州刺史。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed Duke of Anle commandery; held the posts of General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Secretary Honorary Three Excellencies Associate, and Governor of Feng province.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed Duke of Anle, and served as General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Secretary Honorary Three Excellencies Associate, and Governor of Feng province.

sentences.zh: 先穆卒。

translations.literal: He died before Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He died before his father.

sentences.zh: 子筠，襲祖爵。

translations.literal: His son Yun succeeded to the grandfather's title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yun inherited the grandfather's title.

sentences.zh: 惇弟怡，位儀同三司，贈渭州刺史。

translations.literal: Dun's younger brother Yi held the rank of Honorary Three Excellencies Associate; posthumously given Governor of Wei province.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's younger brother Yi held the rank of Honorary Three Excellencies Associate and was posthumously made Governor of Wei province.

sentences.zh: 怡弟雅，少有識量。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Ya from youth had discernment and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Ya showed good judgment even as a youth.

sentences.zh: 仕周，以軍功封西安縣男，位荊州總管。

translations.literal: Serving Zhou, for military merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Xi'an county; held the post of Commander of Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he was enfeoffed Baron of Xi'an for military merit and became Commander of Jing province.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，進爵為公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, he was advanced to Duke.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Kaihuang era he was promoted to duke.

sentences.zh: 雅弟恆，位監州刺史，封曲陽侯。

translations.literal: Ya's younger brother Heng held the post of Governor of Jian province and was enfeoffed Marquis of Quyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ya's younger brother Heng was Governor of Jian province and was enfeoffed Marquis of Quyang.

sentences.zh: 恆弟榮，位合州刺史，長城縣公。

translations.literal: Heng's younger brother Rong held the post of Governor of He province and was Duke of Changcheng county.
translations.idiomatic: Heng's younger brother Rong was Governor of He province and Duke of Changcheng.

sentences.zh: 榮弟直，位車騎將軍、歸政縣侯。

translations.literal: Rong's younger brother Zhi held the post of General of Chariots and Cavalry and was Marquis of Guizheng county.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's younger brother Zhi was General of Chariots and Cavalry and Marquis of Guizheng.

sentences.zh: 直弟雄，位柱國、驃騎將軍、密國公。

translations.literal: Zhi's younger brother Xiong held the posts of Pillar of State and General of Agile Cavalry and was Duke of Mi state.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's younger brother Xiong was Pillar of State, General of Agile Cavalry, and Duke of Mi.

sentences.zh: 雄弟渾，仁壽初，忿筠憢嗇，遣兄子善衡賊之。

translations.literal: Xiong's younger brother Hun—in the beginning of Renshou, resenting Yun's stinginess, sent his elder brother's son Shanheng as assassin against him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong's younger brother Hun—in Renshou's first year, resenting Yun's miserliness—sent his nephew Shanheng to murder him.

sentences.zh: 求盜不得，文帝大怒，盡追其親族。

translations.literal: Seeking the robber-murderer without finding him, Emperor Wen was greatly enraged and pursued all the kin.
translations.idiomatic: When the assassin could not be found, Yang Jian was furious and had the entire clan hunted down.

sentences.zh: 初，筠與從父弟瞿曇有隙，渾遂證瞿曇殺之，而善衡獲免。

translations.literal: Earlier Yun had a rift with his father's younger brother's son Qutan; Hun then testified that Qutan had killed him, and Shanheng was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Yun had long feuded with his cousin Qutan; Hun framed Qutan for the murder, and Shanheng went free.

sentences.zh: 筠死，帝議立嗣。

translations.literal: When Yun died, the emperor deliberated on establishing an heir.
translations.idiomatic: After Yun's death the emperor debated who should inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 邳公蘇威奏筠不軌，請絕其封。

translations.literal: Duke of Pi Su Wei memorialized that Yun had been improper and requested that the enfeoffment be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei, Duke of Pi, reported Yun's misconduct and asked that the line be extinguished.

sentences.zh: 帝不許，乃以渾嗣。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it and therefore had Hun succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and made Hun the heir instead.

sentences.zh: 渾字金才，姿貌瑰偉，美須髯。

translations.literal: Hun, courtesy name Jincai—bearing splendid and towering; beautiful beard and side-whiskers.
translations.idiomatic: Hun, courtesy name Jincai, was imposing in stature, with a splendid beard.

sentences.zh: 起家左侍上士。

translations.literal: He began his career as Left Attendant Senior Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as Left Attendant Senior Clerk.

sentences.zh: 尉遲迥反于鄴，時穆在并州，隋文帝甚慮迥，遣渾乘驛詣穆遽令渾入京奉熨斗曰：「願執柄以慰天下也。」

translations.literal: Yu Chi Jiong rebelled at Ye; at the time Mu was at Bing province; Emperor Wen of Sui greatly worried about Jiong and sent Hun post-haste by courier to Mu, urgently ordering Hun to enter the capital bearing an iron: "May you hold the handle and console all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled at Ye, Li Mu was in Bing province. Yang Jian, deeply worried, sent Hun post-haste to his father with orders to hurry to the capital bearing an iron—"Take the handle and steady the realm.

sentences.zh: 文帝大悅。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian was delighted.

sentences.zh: 又遣渾詣韋孝寬所而述穆意。

translations.literal: He again sent Hun to Wei Xiaokuan's headquarters to convey Mu's meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Hun to Wei Xiaokuan's camp to communicate Li Mu's position.

sentences.zh: 會鄴平，以功授上儀同三司，封安武郡公。

translations.literal: When Ye was pacified, for merit he was granted Senior Honorary Three Excellencies Associate and enfeoffed Duke of Anwu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Ye fell, he was granted Senior Honorary Three Excellencies Associate and enfeoffed Duke of Anwu for his service.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，晉王廣出籓，渾以驃騎將軍領親信，從往揚州。

translations.literal: During Kaihuang, Prince of Jin Guang went out to his fief; Hun as General of Agile Cavalry led trusted followers and followed to Yang province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang era, when Prince Jin Guang left for his post, Hun accompanied him to Yang province as General of Agile Cavalry commanding his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 及筠死，渾規欲紹之，謂妻兄太子左衛率宇文述曰：「若得襲封，當以國賦之半，每歲相奉。」

translations.literal: When Yun died, Hun schemed to succeed him and said to his wife's elder brother Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Left Guard Yuwen Shu: "If I can inherit the enfeoffment, I shall offer half the state's revenue each year in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: After Yun's death Hun schemed to inherit his title and told his brother-in-law Yuwen Shu, commander of the Crown Prince's Left Guard, "If I succeed to the title, I will pay you half the fief's revenue every year.

sentences.zh: 述因入白皇太子，奏文帝，竟詔渾襲申公以奉穆嗣。

translations.literal: Shu thereupon entered and reported to the crown prince, memorialized Emperor Wen, and ultimately an edict had Hun succeed as Duke of Shen to continue Mu's line.
translations.idiomatic: Shu reported to the crown prince and then to Yang Jian, who finally ordered Hun to succeed as Duke of Shen and continue Li Mu's line.

sentences.zh: 大業六年，追改穆封為郕公，渾仍襲焉。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daye, Mu's enfeoffment was posthumously changed to Duke of Cheng; Hun still succeeded to it.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye 6 Li Mu's title was posthumously changed to Duke of Cheng, which Hun continued to hold.

sentences.zh: 累加光祿大夫，遷右驍騎衛大將軍渾既紹父業，日增豪侈。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and transferred to General of the Right Xiaoqi Guard; Hun, having succeeded his father's estate, daily grew more extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and General of the Right Xiaoqi Guard; having inherited his father's wealth, Hun grew daily more extravagant.

sentences.zh: 二歲後不以奉物分述。

translations.literal: After two years he no longer divided the tribute goods with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Within two years he stopped sharing the promised payments with Shu.

sentences.zh: 述大恚，因醉謂其友人于象賢曰：「我竟為金才所賣，死且不忘。」

translations.literal: Shu was greatly enraged; when drunk he said to his friend Yu Xiangxian: "I was ultimately sold out by Jincai—dead I shall not forget it.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was furious; drunk, he told his friend Yu Xiangxian, "That scoundrel Jincai cheated me—I will not forget this even in death.

sentences.zh: 渾聞之，由是結隙。

translations.literal: Hun heard this; from this arose a rift.
translations.idiomatic: Hun heard of it, and from then on they were enemies.

sentences.zh: 及帝討遼東，有方士安伽陀謂帝曰：「李氏應為天子，宜盡誅天下李姓。」

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned against Liaodong, a master of occult arts An Jiatuo said to the emperor: "The Li clan ought to become Sons of Heaven—you should execute all under Heaven surnamed Li.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign, the occultist An Jiatuo told the emperor, "The Li will rule—every person surnamed Li should be killed.

sentences.zh: 述知之，因構渾於帝曰：「臣與金才夙親，聞其數與李敏、善衡等日夜屏語，或終夕不寢。

translations.literal: Shu knew of this and fabricated charges against Hun to the emperor, saying: "Your servant and Jincai have long been close; I hear he repeatedly with Li Min, Shanheng, and others spoke day and night behind closed doors, sometimes not sleeping the whole night.
translations.idiomatic: Shu seized on this and denounced Hun to the emperor: "Jincai and I were once close, but I have heard that he meets Li Min, Shanheng, and others in secret night after night, sometimes until dawn.

sentences.zh: 渾大臣也，家世隆盛，身捉禁兵，不宜然。」

translations.literal: Hun is a great minister; his family for generations has been eminent and prosperous; he personally holds forbidden troops—it is not fitting thus."
translations.idiomatic: Hun is a great minister of an eminent house and commands the palace guard—this is not fitting."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿可覓其事。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You may look into the matter."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Investigate it."

sentences.zh: 述乃遣武賁郎將裴仁基表告渾反，即日遣述掩其家。

translations.literal: Shu then sent Bulwark Commandant Pei Renji to memorialize that Hun had rebelled; that same day he sent Shu to raid his household.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had Bulwark Commandant Pei Renji accuse Hun of treason, and that same day sent men to surround his house.

sentences.zh: 遣左丞元文都、御史大夫裴蘊雜推之，數日，不得反狀。

translations.literal: He sent Left Assistant Yuan Wendu and Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun jointly to investigate; after several days no evidence of rebellion was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Wendu and Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun investigated for days without finding proof of treason.

sentences.zh: 帝更遣述推。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent Shu to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Shu to investigate again.

sentences.zh: 述入獄中召出敏妻宇文氏，謂曰：「夫人，帝甥也，何患無賢夫？

translations.literal: Shu entered the prison and summoned out Min's wife, née Yuwen, and said: "Madam, you are the emperor's niece—what worry is there of lacking a worthy husband?
translations.idiomatic: Shu brought Li Min's wife, Lady Yuwen—the emperor's niece—out of prison and said, "You are the emperor's kin. Would you lack for a worthy husband?

sentences.zh: 李敏、金才名當妖讖，夫人當自求全。」

translations.literal: Li Min and Jincai's names match demonic portents; madam ought to preserve herself.
translations.idiomatic: Li Min and Jincai fit the prophetic curse. Save yourself.

sentences.zh: 因教言金才嘗告敏云：「汝應圖錄，當為天子。

translations.literal: Thereupon he instructed her to say that Jincai had once told Min: "You match the celestial registers—you ought to become Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He coached her to claim that Jincai had told Li Min, "You are marked in the celestial registers to become emperor.

sentences.zh: 今主上好兵，勞擾百姓，此亦天亡隋時也。

translations.literal: Now the sovereign loves warfare and toils and disturbs the common people—this too is Heaven's time for Sui's perishing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's wars have exhausted the people—Heaven intends the Sui to fall.

sentences.zh: 若復度遼，吾與汝必為大將軍，每軍二萬餘兵，固以五萬人矣。

translations.literal: If again crossing to Liaodong, you and I must become great generals—each army twenty-odd thousand troops, fixed at fifty thousand men altogether.
translations.idiomatic: If we campaign against Liaodong again, you and I will command armies of twenty thousand each—fifty thousand men in all.

sentences.zh: 又發諸房子侄內外親婭並募從征，吾家子弟決為主帥，分領兵馬，散在諸軍。

translations.literal: Further, conscripting all the clan's sons, nephews, internal and external affinal kin to follow the campaign, our family's young men would certainly be chief commanders, dividing command of troops and horses, scattered through the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: Our kinsmen will be conscripted for the campaign; our clan's young men will command troops embedded in every army.

sentences.zh: 吾懷汝前發，襲取御營，子弟響赴，一日之間，天下定矣。」

translations.literal: I embrace you and move first, seizing the imperial camp; sons and nephews respond and converge—in the space of one day all under Heaven is settled."
translations.idiomatic: We strike first at the imperial camp; our kin will rally—and in a single day the realm is ours."

sentences.zh: 述口自傳授，令敏妻寫表，封云「上密」。

translations.literal: Shu himself orally dictated; he had Min's wife write the memorial, sealed it "Secret for the Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Shu dictated the confession and had Li Min's wife write it into a memorial sealed "Secret for the Emperor."

sentences.zh: 述持入奏云：「已得金才反狀，並有敏妻密表。」

translations.literal: Shu brought it in and memorialized, saying: "I have already obtained Jincai's evidence of rebellion, together with Min's wife's secret memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Shu presented it to the throne: "I have proof of Jincai's treason and Lady Li's secret memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝覽之，泣曰：「吾宗社幾傾，賴親家公而獲全耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor perused it and wept, saying: "My altars of soil and grain nearly toppled—it is by relying on my father-in-law that I was preserved whole."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and wept. "The realm nearly fell—only my father-in-law Yuwen Shu saved it."

sentences.zh: 於是誅渾、敏等，自餘無少長皆徙嶺表。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hun, Min, and others were executed; all the rest, old and young alike, were banished to Ling's frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Hun, Li Min, and the rest were executed; everyone else in the clan, young and old, was exiled to the southern frontier.

sentences.zh: 睿字恃德，少沉敏有行檢。

translations.literal: Rui, courtesy name Shide—in youth was deep, keen, and had conduct and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Rui, courtesy name Shide, was thoughtful and quick-witted from youth, with firm moral discipline.

sentences.zh: 周文帝時，以功臣子養宮中，復命與諸子遊。

translations.literal: During Emperor Wen of Zhou, as a meritorious minister's son he was raised in the palace; again he was ordered to keep company with the princes.
translations.idiomatic: In the time of Emperor Wen of Zhou he was reared in the palace as the son of a meritorious minister and was allowed to play with the princes.

sentences.zh: 七歲，襲爵廣平郡公。

translations.literal: At seven years, he succeeded to the title Duke of Guangping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At age seven he inherited the title Duke of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 累加儀同三司、本州大中正、開府，改封五龍郡公，渭州刺史。

translations.literal: He was cumulatively given Honorary Three Excellencies Associate, Chief Rectifier of his native prefecture, and Opening the Government; his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Wulong commandery, and he was appointed Governor of Wei province.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Honorary Three Excellencies Associate, made chief rectifier of his home prefecture, and granted an open office; his title was changed to Duke of Wulong, and he was appointed governor of Wei province.

sentences.zh: 周閔帝受禪，徵為禦伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min of Zhou received the abdication, Rui was summoned to be Imperial Bearer.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min of Zhou took the throne, Rui was recalled to serve as Imperial Bearer.

sentences.zh: 出為中州刺史，鎮新安以備齊。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Zhong province, garrisoning Xin'an to guard against Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as governor of Zhong province, garrisoning Xin'an against Qi.

sentences.zh: 齊人來寇，睿輒挫之。

translations.literal: When Qi men came to raid, Rui at once repulsed them.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi raiders attacked, Rui beat them back at once.

sentences.zh: 帝甚嘉歎，拜大將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly praised and sighed in admiration, appointing him Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him warmly and made him Grand General.

sentences.zh: 以禦佐命功，進爵蔣國公。

translations.literal: For Yu's merit in assisting the founding mandate, he was advanced in rank to Duke of the State of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: For Liang Yu's merit in helping establish the dynasty, he was promoted to Duke of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 入為司會。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Director of Accounts.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as Director of Accounts.

sentences.zh: 後從齊王憲拒齊將斛律明月於洛陽，每戰有功，遷小塚宰。

translations.literal: Later he followed Prince of Qi Xian in resisting Qi general Hulu Mingyue at Luoyang; in every battle he had merit, and was transferred to Junior Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Prince Xian of Qi against the Qi general Hulu Mingyue at Luoyang, distinguishing himself in every engagement, and was appointed Junior Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 曆敷州刺史、涼、安二州總管，俱有惠政，進位柱國。

translations.literal: He successively served as Governor of Fu province and as area commander of the two provinces of Liang and An; in both there were benevolent policies, and he was advanced to Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: He served as governor of Fu and as area commander of Liang and An, earning a reputation for good government in both posts, and was promoted to Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝總百揆，代王謙為益州總管。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui held all the hundred offices, he replaced Wang Qian as area commander of Yi province.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian assumed control of the government, Rui replaced Wang Qian as area commander of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 行至漢川西，謙反，攻始州，睿不得進。

translations.literal: When he reached west of Hanchuan, Qian rebelled, attacked Shizhou, and Rui could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Rui had reached the western Han River when Wang Qian rebelled, attacked Shizhou, and blocked his advance.

sentences.zh: 文帝命睿為行軍元帥，率行軍總管于義、張威、達奚長儒、梁升、石孝義步騎二十萬討之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen ordered Rui to be campaign commander-in-chief and to lead campaign commanders Yu Yi, Zhang Wei, Daxi Changru, Liang Sheng, and Shi Xiaoyi with two hundred thousand infantry and cavalry to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian appointed Rui campaign commander-in-chief and sent him with two hundred thousand foot and horse soldiers under the generals Yu Yi, Zhang Wei, Daxi Changru, Liang Sheng, and Shi Xiaoyi to crush the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 謙遣開府李三王守通穀，睿使張威擊破之。

translations.literal: Qian sent open-office holder Li Sanwang to hold Tonggu; Rui had Zhang Wei strike and defeat him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qian sent Li Sanwang to hold Tonggu Pass; Rui ordered Zhang Wei to break the position.

sentences.zh: 進至龍門，謙將趙儼、秦會擁眾十萬，據險為營，周亙三十里。

translations.literal: Advancing to Longmen, Qian's generals Zhao Yan and Qin Hui mustered a host of one hundred thousand, occupied steep ground and made camps, encircling thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: At Longmen, Wang Qian's generals Zhao Yan and Qin Hui massed a hundred thousand men in fortified camps along the defiles, stretching some thirty li.

sentences.zh: 睿令將士銜枚，出自間道，四面奮擊，力戰破之，遂鼓行而進。

translations.literal: Rui ordered officers and soldiers, with gag-sticks in their mouths, to emerge by hidden paths, strike fiercely on four sides, fight with all their strength and break them, then advance to the beat of drums.
translations.idiomatic: Rui sent his men along hidden paths with gag-sticks in their mouths, struck from all sides at once, broke the enemy line after fierce fighting, and marched forward to the beat of drums.

sentences.zh: 謙將敬豪守劍閣，梁岩拒平林，並懼而來降。

translations.literal: Qian's general Jing Hao guarded Jian'ge, and Liang Yan held Pinglin; both, in fear, came and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qian's officers Jing Hao at Jian'ge and Liang Yan at Pinglin both surrendered in fear.

sentences.zh: 謙又命高阿那瑰、達奚惎等以盛兵攻利州。

translations.literal: Qian again ordered Gao Anagong, Daxi Ji, and others with a mighty army to attack Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qian then sent Gao Anagong, Daxi Ji, and others with a large force against Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 聞睿將至，颭分兵據開遠。

translations.literal: Hearing that Rui was about to arrive, Ji divided his troops and occupied Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Daxi Ji learned that Rui was approaching, he split his force and seized Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 睿遣上開府拓拔宗趣、劍閣大將軍宇文瓊指巴西，大將軍趙達水軍入嘉陵。

translations.literal: Rui sent Senior Opening-the-Fu Tuoba Zong to hurry toward Jian'ge, Jian'ge Grand General Yuwen Qiong toward Baxi, and Grand General Zhao Da with a water army into the Jialing.
translations.idiomatic: Rui sent Tuoba Zong toward Jian'ge, Yuwen Qiong toward Baxi, and Zhao Da with a river fleet up the Jialing.

sentences.zh: 遣張威、王倫、賀若震、于義、韓相貴、阿那惠等分道攻惎，自午及申，破之。

translations.literal: He sent Zhang Wei, Wang Lun, He Ruo Zhen, Yu Yi, Han Xianggui, Anahui, and others by separate routes to attack Ji; from the hour wu until the hour shen he defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhang Wei, Wang Lun, He Ruo Zhen, Yu Yi, Han Xianggui, Anahui, and others against Ji by separate routes and broke his force between noon and dusk.

sentences.zh: 惎奔歸於謙。

translations.literal: Ji fled in flight and returned to Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Ji fled back to Wang Qian.

sentences.zh: 睿逼成都，謙令達奚惎、乙弗虔守城，親帥精兵五萬，背城結陳。

translations.literal: Rui pressed on Chengdu; Qian ordered Daxi Ji and Yifu Qian to hold the city in defense, personally leading fifty thousand crack troops and, with their backs to the city, forming battle lines.
translations.idiomatic: Rui pressed on toward Chengdu. Wang Qian ordered Daxi Ji and Yifu Qian to hold the city while he personally led fifty thousand elite troops and drew up his battle line with the walls at his back.

sentences.zh: 睿擊敗之。

translations.literal: Rui struck and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Rui defeated him.

sentences.zh: 謙將入城，惎、虔以城降。

translations.literal: Qian was about to enter the city; Ji and Qian surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qian was about to enter the city, but Ji and Qian surrendered it.

sentences.zh: 謙將麾下三十騎遁走，新都令王寶執之，睿斬謙於市，劍南悉平。

translations.literal: Qian, with thirty riders from his retinue, fled away; Wang Bao, magistrate of Xindu, seized him; Rui executed Qian in the marketplace, and all of Jiannan was fully pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qian escaped with thirty horsemen from his personal guard; Wang Bao, magistrate of Xindu, captured him; Rui executed Wang Qian in the marketplace, and all of Jiannan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 進位上柱國，總管如故，賜物五千段、奴婢一千口、金二千兩、銀三千兩，邑千戶。

translations.literal: He was promoted in rank to Supreme Pillar of State; his post as area commander remained as before; he was granted five thousand bolts of goods, one thousand slaves and servants, two thousand taels of gold, three thousand taels of silver, and a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Rui was promoted to Senior Pillar of State while retaining his command; he received five thousand bolts of goods, a thousand slaves and servants, two thousand taels of gold, three thousand taels of silver, and a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 睿時威振西州，夷獠歸附，唯南寧首帥爨震恃遠不賓。

translations.literal: At this time Rui's authority shook the western provinces; the Yi and Liao submitted, but only Cuan Zhen, chieftain of Nanning, relying on the distance, did not pay court.
translations.idiomatic: By then Rui's prestige dominated the western provinces; the Yi and Liao peoples submitted, but Cuan Zhen, chieftain of Nanning, alone relied on his remoteness and refused allegiance.

sentences.zh: 睿上疏曰：「南寧州，漢牂柯之地。

translations.literal: Rui submitted a memorial, saying: "Nanning Prefecture was the land of Zangke in Han.
translations.idiomatic: Rui submitted a memorial: "Nanning Prefecture was Zangke territory in Han times.

sentences.zh: 近代已來，分置興古、雲南、建寧、硃提四郡，戶口殷眾，金寶富饒，二河有駿馬明珠，益、寧出鹽井犀角。

translations.literal: From recent times onward, it was divided and set up as the four commanderies of Xinggu, Yunnan, Jianning, and Zhuti; registered households are numerous and dense; gold and treasure are rich and abundant; the Two Rivers have fine horses and luminous pearls; Yi and Ning produce salt wells and rhinoceros horns.
translations.idiomatic: In recent generations it has been divided into the four commanderies of Xinggu, Yunnan, Jianning, and Zhuti. Its population is dense, its gold and treasure abundant; the Two Rivers yield fine horses and luminous pearls; Yizhou and Ning produce salt wells and rhinoceros horn.

sentences.zh: 晉泰始七年以益州曠遠，分置寧州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taishi of Jin, because Yizhou was vast and remote, Ning Prefecture was separately established.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Jin Taishi era, because Yizhou was vast and remote, Ning Prefecture was established separately.

sentences.zh: 至偽梁，南寧州刺史徐文盛被湘東征赴荊州。

translations.literal: Down to the false Liang, Xu Wensheng, Inspector of Nanning, was summoned by Xiangdong for a campaign to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: This continued until Xu Wensheng, inspector of Nanning under the puppet Liang, was summoned by Xiangdong to march on Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 屬東夏尚阻，未遑遠略，土人爨瓚遂竊據一方。

translations.literal: At that time the eastern realm was still obstructed, and there was no leisure for distant strategy; the local man Cuan Zan then seized and occupied one region.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern lands were still unsettled, and the court had no leisure for distant campaigns; the local leader Cuan Zan then seized the region for himself.

sentences.zh: 國家遙授刺史，其子震相承至今。

translations.literal: The state appointed him inspector from afar; his son Zhen has succeeded him down to the present.
translations.idiomatic: The court confirmed him as inspector from afar, and his son Zhen has held power in succession down to the present day.

sentences.zh: 而震臣禮多虧，貢賦不入。

translations.literal: Yet Zhen is deficient in the observance of ministerial rites; tribute and levies do not enter the court.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhen falls far short in vassal propriety, and tribute and taxes never reach the court.

sentences.zh: 如聞彼人苦其苛政，思被皇風幸因平蜀士眾，不煩重興師旅，狎獠既訖，即請略定南寧。」

translations.literal: As I have heard, the people there suffer under harsh government and long to be covered by the imperial wind; fortunately, with the troops that have pacified Shu, one need not trouble to raise armies anew — once the Liao are subdued, I request to pacify Nanning in brief."
translations.idiomatic: I hear that the people there suffer under harsh rule and long to come under the emperor's benevolent sway; with the army that has just pacified Shu, there is no need to raise new forces — once the tribal peoples are brought under control, I ask to move swiftly to settle Nanning.

sentences.zh: 文帝深納之，然以天下初定，恐人心不安，故未之許。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen deeply accepted it, yet because the realm had just been settled, fearing that hearts would not be at ease, he therefore did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian approved the plan in principle, but with the realm only newly settled he feared unsettling public opinion and did not grant permission.

sentences.zh: 後竟遣史萬歲討平之，並因睿之策也。

translations.literal: Later he finally sent Shi Wansui to attack and pacify it — also following Rui's strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shi Wansui was sent to pacify the region, following Rui's strategy.

sentences.zh: 睿威惠兼著，人夷悅服，聲望逾重，文帝陰憚之。

translations.literal: Rui's authority and benevolence were both manifest; the people and the Yi were pleased and submitted; his repute and prestige grew ever heavier; Emperor Wen secretly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's power and benevolence were equally felt; Han and tribal peoples alike were won over, and his prestige grew until Yang Jian began to fear him in secret.

sentences.zh: 薛道衡從軍在蜀，說睿勸進，文帝大悅。

translations.literal: Xue Daheng, having followed the army in Shu, urged Rui to counsel accession to the throne; Emperor Wen was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Daheng, who had accompanied the army in Shu, persuaded Rui to urge Yang Jian to take the throne, and Yang Jian was delighted.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，顧待彌隆。

translations.literal: When Yang Jian accepted the abdication, his regard and favor grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian accepted the abdication, his regard and favor toward Rui grew ever greater.

sentences.zh: 睿復上平陳策，帝善之，下詔曰：「昔公孫、隗囂，漢之賊也，光武與其通和，稱為皇帝。

translations.literal: Rui again submitted a plan for conquering Chen; the emperor approved and issued an edict, saying: "Formerly Gongsun Shu and Wei Xiao were enemies of Han, yet Emperor Guangwu exchanged peace with them and called them emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Rui again submitted a plan for conquering Chen. The emperor approved it and issued an edict: "In the past Gongsun Shu and Wei Xiao were enemies of Han, yet Emperor Guangwu treated with them and addressed them as emperors.

sentences.zh: 佗之于高祖，初猶不臣。

translations.literal: Zhao Tuo toward Emperor Gaozu at first still did not submit as a vassal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tuo at first refused to submit to Emperor Gaozu of Han.

sentences.zh: 孫皓之答晉文，書尚雲'白'。

translations.literal: When Sun Hao replied to Emperor Wen of Jin, his letter still used the character 'bai'.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Hao replied to Emperor Wen of Jin, his letter still used plain 'bai' — the informal second-person pronoun.

sentences.zh: 或尋款服，或即滅亡。

translations.literal: Some soon submitted with sincerity; some were immediately destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Some soon submitted in good faith; others were swiftly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 王者體大，義存遵養，雖陳國來朝，示盡蕃節，如公大略，誠須責罪，尚欲且緩其誅，宜如此意。

translations.literal: A sage king's stature is great; the principle is to preserve and nurture; though Chen has come to court, showing complete vassal propriety — by your grand plan, guilt would indeed need to be prosecuted, yet I still wish for the time being to delay their punishment; you should understand this intention.
translations.idiomatic: A true king's stature is great, and the principle is to nurture rather than destroy. Though Chen has sent envoys to court, your plan would indeed call for punishment — yet I still wish to delay action for the present. You should understand my meaning.

sentences.zh: 淮海未滅，必興師旅，若命永襲，終當相屈，以身許國，無足致辭也。」

translations.literal: When Huai-Hai has not yet been destroyed, armies must be raised; if you are ordered to take the field, in the end you will surely be called upon; devoting your person to the state, there is no need for further words."
translations.idiomatic: When the Huai-Hai region has yet to be conquered, troops will surely be raised; when you are ordered to take the field, you will in the end be called upon — devote yourself to the state with your whole being; there is no need to say more.

sentences.zh: 睿乃止。

translations.literal: Rui then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Rui then dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 睿時見突厥方強，恐為邊患，復陳鎮守之策十餘事。

translations.literal: At this time Rui saw that the Turks were growing strong and feared they would become a border menace; he again set forth more than ten measures for garrison defense.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the Turks were growing strong and fearing a border threat, Rui submitted more than ten measures for frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉歎久之，答以厚意。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and sighed over it for a long time and replied with warm regard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised it at length and replied with warm appreciation.

sentences.zh: 睿時自以周代舊臣，久居重鎮，內不自安，屢請入朝，於是征還京師。

translations.literal: At this time Rui, considering himself an old minister of the Zhou, long stationed in a weighty post, felt inwardly ill at ease and repeatedly requested to come to court; thereupon he was summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Rui, considering himself an old minister of the Zhou who had long held a weighty frontier post, felt uneasy and repeatedly asked to come to court; he was then summoned back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 及引見，上為之興，命睿升殿，握手極歡。

translations.literal: When he was granted an audience, the emperor rose for him, ordered Rui to ascend the hall, and clasped his hand in the greatest cordiality.
translations.idiomatic: When he was granted an audience, the emperor rose to receive him, had Rui ascend the hall, and clasped his hand in warm greeting.

sentences.zh: 睿退謂所親曰：「功遂身退，今其時也。」

translations.literal: Rui withdrew and said to those close to him: "When merit is achieved, the person withdraws — now is the time."
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Rui told those close to him: "When the work is done, withdraw — now is the time.

sentences.zh: 遂謝病，闔門自守，不交當時。

translations.literal: Thereupon he pleaded illness, shut his gates and kept to himself, and had no dealings with men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He then pleaded illness, shut his gates, and kept aloof from public affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝賜以板輿，每有朝覲，必令三衛輿上殿。

translations.literal: The emperor granted him a palanquin; whenever there was a court audience, he invariably ordered the Three Guards to carry him up to the hall in it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him a palanquin, and whenever he came to court, the Three Guards were ordered to carry him up to the hall.

sentences.zh: 睿初平王謙之始，自以威名太盛，恐為時所忌，遂大受金賄以自穢。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Rui had first pacified Wang Qian, considering that his prestige and fame were too great and fearing that the age would be jealous of him, he therefore accepted large bribes in gold to defile himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Rui had first pacified Wang Qian, he feared that his fame was too great and would excite jealousy, and so he deliberately accepted large bribes to tarnish his own reputation.

sentences.zh: 由是勳簿多不以實，詣朝堂稱屈者，前後百數人。

translations.literal: Because of this, the rolls of merit often did not accord with fact; those who came to the court hall claiming injustice numbered a hundred or more, before and after.
translations.idiomatic: As a result, the rolls of merit often did not reflect actual deeds, and more than a hundred men came before the court to protest injustice.

sentences.zh: 上令有司案驗其事，主者多獲罪。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the relevant offices to investigate and verify the matter; those chiefly responsible mostly received punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the relevant offices to investigate, and many of those chiefly responsible were punished.

sentences.zh: 睿懼，上表陳謝，請歸大理。

translations.literal: Rui was fearful; he submitted a memorial expressing regret and asked to be handed over to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Rui was alarmed, submitted a memorial of apology, and asked to be handed over to the judicial authorities.

sentences.zh: 上慰喻遣之。

translations.literal: The emperor comforted and instructed him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted him and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 十五年，從至洛陽而卒，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he followed the emperor to Luoyang and died; his posthumous title was Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he accompanied the emperor to Luoyang and died; he was given the posthumous title Xiang.

sentences.zh: 子洋嗣，歷位嵩徐二州刺史、武賁郎將。

translations.literal: His son Yang succeeded him and successively held the posts of Governor of the two provinces of Song and Xu and Bulwark Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yang succeeded him and served as governor of Song and Xu provinces and as a commander of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 大業六年，詔追改睿封為戴公，命以洋襲焉。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daye, an edict retroactively changed Rui's enfeoffment to Duke of Dai and ordered that Yang inherit it.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye 6 an edict retroactively changed Rui's title to Duke of Dai and ordered that Yang inherit the rank.

sentences.zh: 論曰：賀拔嶽變起倉卒，侯莫陳悅意在兼併，于時人有離心，士無固志。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Heba Yue's revolt arose in sudden haste; Hou Mo Chen Yue's intent lay in absorption and annexation; at the time people had hearts of separation, soldiers had no firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Heba Yue's disaster erupted in an instant; Hou Mo Chen Yue meant to absorb his power; men's loyalty wavered and the army's will was unsteady.

sentences.zh: 寇洛撫循散亂，抗禦仇讎，全師而還，敵人絕覬覦之望；

translations.literal: Kou Luo soothed and guided the scattered disorder, resisted and repelled the enemy avengers, returned with the whole army intact, and the foe cut off all covetous hopes;
translations.idiomatic: Kou Luo rallied a broken army, held off the avenging foe, and brought his troops home intact, ending the enemy's hopes at a stroke;

sentences.zh: 度德而處，霸王建匡合之謀。

translations.literal: Weighing virtue and so acting, he helped the hegemon-king establish the plan of uniting the realm.
translations.idiomatic: measuring the times and acting accordingly, he helped his lord conceive the strategy of uniting the empire.

sentences.zh: 趙貴居二闕之險，周室定二分之功。

translations.literal: Zhao Gui held the peril of the Two Passes; the Zhou house settled the merit of dividing Wei in two.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gui held the Two Passes' vital ground and helped the Zhou secure the partition of Wei;

sentences.zh: 彼此一時，其功固不細也。

translations.literal: Each in his own time — their merit was indeed no small thing.
translations.idiomatic: each served his moment — and neither man's achievement was small.

sentences.zh: 李賢和兄弟屬亂離之際，居戎馬之間，志略從橫，忠勇奮發，頻摧勍敵，屢涉艱危。

translations.literal: Li Xian and his brothers belonged to an age of disorder and separation, dwelt amid war-horses; their resolve and stratagems ranged far and wide, loyalty and courage blazed forth, frequently crushing formidable foes, repeatedly passing through hardship and peril.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian and his brothers came of age in chaos and war; their minds were bold and far-ranging, their loyalty and courage unmistakable; again and again they broke strong enemies and passed through mortal danger.

sentences.zh: 及逢時遇主，策名委質，荷生成之恩，蒙國士之遇，俱縻好爵，各著勳庸。

translations.literal: When they met the time and encountered their lord, they registered their names and pledged their substance, bore the grace of having life given them, received treatment as knights of the state, all were bound with fine ranks, each achieved distinguished merit.
translations.idiomatic: When fortune brought them to their lord, they pledged their service, owed him their lives, and were honored as his most trusted men; each won high rank and a name for achievement.

sentences.zh: 遂得任兼文武，聲彰出內，位高望重，光國榮家，跗萼連暉，聊椒繁衍，冠冕之盛，當時莫與比焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon they attained office combining civil and military roles, fame manifest inside and out, rank high and repute heavy, illuminating the state and honoring the clan; like calyxes and petals linked in splendor, like pepper-sprays spreading abroad — the glory of caps and crowns, none in the age could be compared with them.
translations.idiomatic: They came to hold civil and military authority alike; their fame reached court and camp; high in rank and heavy in prestige, they brought glory to their house and their dynasty; their kin spread and flourished like linked blossoms — no clan in the age matched their splendor.

sentences.zh: 自周迄隋，鬱為西京盛族，雖金、張在漢，不之尚也。

translations.literal: From Zhou through Sui, they flourished as the great clan of the Western Capital; though the Jin and Zhang of Han were esteemed, they would not be placed above this.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhou through the Sui they were the great house of the western capital; even the Jin and Zhang clans of Han could not match them.

sentences.zh: 然而周文始崩，嗣君沖幼，內則功臣放命，外則強寇臨邊，晉公以猶子之親，膺負圖之托，遂能撫甯家國，開翦異端，革魏興周，遠安邇悅，功勤已著，過惡未彰。

translations.literal: Yet when Yuwen Wen first died, the successor lord was young and tender; within, meritorious ministers presumptuously ordered affairs; without, strong foemen pressed the borders; the Duke of Jin, through the intimacy of a nephew-like kin, received the entrustment of the dynastic design; thereby he could soothe and settle state and family, open and cut away heterodox factions, change Wei and raise Zhou, pacify the distant and please the near — merit and exertion were already manifest, faults and evils not yet revealed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Yuwen Tai died, the heir was still a child; within, the great ministers grew unruly, while without, enemies pressed the frontier. Yuwen Hu, as the founder's kinsman, took up the burden of the throne; he settled the realm, suppressed rivals, replaced Wei with Zhou, and won men near and far — his service was plain, his faults not yet exposed.

sentences.zh: 李植受遇先朝，宿參機務，慮威權之去已，懼將來之不容，生此厲階，成茲貝錦，乃以小謀大，由疏間親。

translations.literal: Li Zhi had received favor from the former court, long participated in secret affairs, feared that authority and power would leave him, dreaded that the future would not contain him; from this arose the stair of calamity, from this was formed the brocade of slander; thus with small status he plotted against great, from estrangement he drove a wedge between kin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi, favored in the previous reign and long privy to state secrets, feared losing power and being destroyed in turn; he opened the way to disaster and wove false accusations — a lesser man scheming against a greater, a distant relation driving wedges among kin.

sentences.zh: 主無昭帝之明，臣有上官之訴，嫌隙既兆，釁故因之，啟塚宰無君之心，成閔帝廢弑之禍，植之由也。

translations.literal: The lord lacked Emperor Zhao's discernment; the minister had Shangguan's plea — once suspicion and rifts had appeared, causes for conflict followed; this opened the Minister of State's heart of disloyalty to his lord, and brought about the disaster of Emperor Min's deposition and murder — through Li Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler lacked Emperor Zhao's clear sight; the minister had his grievance like Shangguan Junde — once suspicion opened a rift, rebellion followed; the regent's disloyalty was unleashed, and Emperor Min was deposed and killed — all through Li Zhi.

sentences.zh: 李遠闕義方之訓，又無先見之明，以至誅夷，非為不幸。

translations.literal: Li Yuan lacked instruction in the righteousness of the way, and also lacked foresight; that he came to execution and extermination was no misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan had neither his family's moral guidance nor foresight; that he was executed was hardly undeserved.

sentences.zh: 梁禦豫奉興王，參謀締構，驅馳畢力，夷險備嘗，雖遠志未申，亦云遇其時矣。

translations.literal: Liang Yu from the first served the founding king, counselled in the founding structure, raced and exerted his full strength, prepared to meet both ease and peril, though his far-reaching resolve was not fulfilled — it may still be said that he met his time.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yu early served the founding king, helped shape the new order, and gave his full strength through every hardship; though his larger ambitions went unrealized, he still met his moment.

sentences.zh: 穆及梁睿皆周室功臣，隋文王業初基，俱受腹心之寄，故穆首登師傅，睿終膺殊寵，觀其見機而動，抑亦人之先覺。

translations.literal: Mu and Liang Rui were both meritorious ministers of the Zhou house; when Emperor Wen of Sui's royal enterprise was first founded, both received the trust of his innermost heart; therefore Mu was first elevated to Grand Tutor, and Rui in the end received extraordinary favor; observing how they perceived the moment and acted, they may also be called men who foresaw ahead of others.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu and Liang Rui were Zhou founding ministers; when Yang Jian's empire was first taking shape, both held his deepest trust — Mu was raised first to Grand Tutor, Rui received extraordinary favor at the end. In reading how they read the moment and acted, they rank among those who see ahead of others.

sentences.zh: 然方魏朝之貞烈，有愧王淩，比晉室之忠臣，終慚徐廣。

translations.literal: Yet compared with the steadfast martyrs of the Wei court, they must feel shame before Wang Ling; compared with the loyal ministers of the Jin house, they must in the end feel shame before Xu Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Yet measured against the steadfast martyrs of Wei, they must feel shame before Wang Ling; measured against the loyal ministers of Jin, they must in the end feel shame before Xu Guang.

sentences.zh: 穆之子孫，特為隆盛，硃輪華轂，凡數十人，見忌當時，禍難遄及，得之非道，可不戒歟？

translations.literal: Mu's sons and grandsons were especially flourishing in grandeur; those with vermilion wheel hubs and ornate carriage shafts numbered several tens. Envied by the age, disaster swiftly reached them — gains obtained by improper means: can one not take warning!
translations.idiomatic: Mu's descendants flourished beyond measure — several dozen of them rode in carriages with vermilion wheels and ornate hubs. Resented by their contemporaries, disaster swiftly overtook them. Wealth gained by improper means — is this not a lesson to heed?
